Identifies the parent model in the Model hierarchy. This property provides the configured revision of model object referred by cfg0ParentThread property which is present in the current model object as per the application configurations.

Specifies list of combined Feature revisions which define the current product line object along with roll-down features starting from its immediate parent to all the way up to the root node in the model hierarchy.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsModelFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsFamily. It serves as a Family for model Features.User can create a configuration model family and attach it with the Cfg0ProductItem using the attribute cfg0OwningProductItem.

The Cfg0AbsModelFamilyThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsModelFamily object.A Cfg0AbsModelFamily object has cfg0OwningProductItem attribute which is independent of its revisions. It cannot be changed once the object is saved.

The Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSO is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO. It is a super class of all product configurator rule objects such as constraint rules or default rules.The Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSO defines its applicability to the Cfg0ConfContext Items with attribute cfg0ProductItems. It also holds the references of product configurator option objects which contribute to the expression attached to it. These references serve the whereUsed search on the option objects.
The Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSOThrd is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSOThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSO object.
The Cfg0AbsModelThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsModel object.

The Cfg0AbsOptionFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsFamily.The Cfg0AbsOptionFamily helps user to define the variant configuration options and also specify the minimum and maximum values for the options. For example, user wants to provide different length options for his product 5 feet, 10 feet and 15 feet. User can create an integer Cfg0AbsOptionFamily say Length and associate it with the Cfg0ConfContext Item such as Cfg0ProductItem or Cfg0Dictionary. Then, user can define the above Features linked to the family. User also specifies the minimum value as 5 feet and maximum value as 15 feet for the family.

TcProperty.description: Specifies the maximum allowed value for the family. The value must be of the same data type as that of family. The maximum value acts as a constraint to validate the product configurations which consume the family.

Specifies the minimum allowed value for the family. The value must be of the same data type as that of family. The minimum value acts as a constraint to validate the product configurations which consume the family.
Specifies the list of Cfg0ConfContext Items to which Family is allocated. It helps in whereUsed use cases for the family.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsOptionFamilyThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsOptionFamily object.

The Cfg0AbsOptionValue is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsValue. It represents the variant configuration options to user.The Cfg0AbsOptionValue helps user to represent the non-model variant configuration options. It also helps to identify the family to which the feature is linked. The Cfg0AbsOptionValue returns information to user such as what are the compound Features which summarizes or packages the Feature. For example, user can create a Feature Summary as 'Low Size Products' and add Features 5 feet and 10 feet as members to it. It also returns the family object and family id to which the Feature is attached.

TcProperty.description: Specifies the Family revision to which feature object is attached to.
Specifies the Cfg0ConfContext Items in which this Feature is allocated.
Specifies the Feature Package revisions which have this Feature as its member.
Specifies the Feature Summary revisions which summarize the Feature.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsOptionValueThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsOptionValue object.
The Cfg0AbsPackageFamilyThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsCompoundFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsPackageFamily object.
The Cfg0AbsPackageOptionFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsCompoundValueFamily. It facilitates creation of compound variant configuration options such as a package of Features.

The Cfg0AbsPackageOptionValue is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsCompoundOptionValue. It represents compound variant configuration options such as a package of Features.The Cfg0AbsPackageOptionValue helps user to represent the conjunction of Features. For example, for the product Car, to create a Navigation package of Features like GPS Receiver, Electronic Compass and LCD Display, user can create a Navigation Feature Package as instance of a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageOptionValue with options GPS Receiver, Electronic Compass and LCD Display as packaged members. During validation of the product configurations, the Feature Packages function as constraints. The selection of Feature Package 'Navigation Package' expands to a package constraint as 'Navigation Package AND GPS Receiver AND Electronic Compass AND LCD Display '. It generates validation error if the package constraint is not met.

The Cfg0AbsPackageRule is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConstraintRule. It defines a configurator constraint rule for dependency of Package Features in a product configuration. The Cfg0AbsPackageRule helps user to express a positive validity restriction to a combination of Features in a product configuration. Invalid product configuration violating this package rule, the message and severity of the violated rule is returned to user. The product configuration is evaluated against all such configurator constraints applicable to the product to determine if it is a valid or invalid configuration and update the configuration if necessary to make it a valid one. Subject condition of Package Rule should be always a single CNF. Each clause of CNF may have alternatives. Defaults for alternatives of a clauses is defined through default condition property. Alternatives are mutually exclusive with applicability condition of rule object. For example, SafetyPackage Feature with applicability as Model=M1 has two clauses as AirBag, ABS. AirBag has alternative as 2 or 4 or 6 where 4 is default. ABS has alternative as 3Wheel or 4Wheel where 3Wheel is default. Default condition will be 'AirBag=4 & ABS=3Wheel'.

TcProperty.description: cfg0PackageFeature is runtime typed referenced property which represents a revision of Package Feature for which Package variant is defined as rule object. Package Feature allows to query all package features which has variation in a given product context. cfg0PackageFeature provides a configured revisions of value referred by cfg0PackageFeatureThread for current Package Rule object per Configurator Perspective.

cfg0DefaultCondition is runtime string property which represents expression for defaults in alternatives of a expression clauses. For example, SafetyPackage Feature with applicability as Model=M1 has two clauses as AirBag, ABS. AirBag has alternative as 2 or 4 or 6 where 4 is default. ABS has alternative as 3Wheel or 4Wheel where 3Wheel is default. Default condition will be 'AirBag=4 & ABS=3Wheel'.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsPackageRuleThrd is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConstraintRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsPackageRule object.
The Cfg0AbsPackageValueThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsCompoundValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsPackageOptionValue object.
The Cfg0AbsProdModelFamilyThrd is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsProductModelFamily object.

The Cfg0AbsProductLine is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModel. It defines a set of product models with a common business strategy.The Cfg0AbsProductLine can be used in constraint rules and/or variant conditions to enforce a consistent relationship with technology options and solutions across all product models represented by this product line. For example, user has Power Supply as a product with two product variants viz. Uninterruptible Power Supply and Inverter. Here, user can create the product line option like 'Power Supply Product Line' under the generic product context Power Supply. The product line option can then cater to the common characteristics of Uninterruptible Power Supply and Inverter. The Battery option for power supply could be such a common characteristic. The Cfg0AbsProductLine is used to represent series of product models. It is less detailed, less precise compared to product models. Multiple product models could be covered by single product line.

TcProperty.description: Specifies list of Feature revisions which define current product line object.

Returns precise product models which are covered by current product line object. The product line and product models do not have any direct relation. The members of product models also define the product line and based on the commonality, the product models for a product line are identified.
Deprecated: This Property has been deprecated tc12.3 onwards. Please use Cfg0AbsModel::cfg0characteristics instead.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsProductLineFamThrd is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsProductLineFamily object.
The Cfg0AbsProductLineFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamily. It represents the family for the product line Features.
The Cfg0AbsProductLineThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsProductLine object.

The Cfg0AbsProductModel is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModel. It represents an elemental product model Feature.The Cfg0AbsProductModel helps user to link a business strategy for a product to its technology configuration options. For example, to provide different model options for his product say Car as Economy and Luxury, user can create an instance of concrete type of Cfg0AbsProductModelFamily and attaches it with the Cfg0ProductItem. Then, user can define the above model Features linked to the family. The product model values are always specific to a product and hence, they are attached to a single Cfg0ProductItem. The allocations and family groups are not supported for a Cfg0AbsProductModel. User can assign members to a Cfg0AbsProductModel. For example, an Economy product model can have member options as Fuel Capacity=1 liter, Body Style=Hatchback and Transmission=Manual. In order to define a member option, it must be made available to the model. The member options like Fuel Capacity=1 liter, Body Style=Hatchback and Transmission=Manual function as a constraint in product configuration validations.

TcProperty.description: Specifies the list of Feature revisions which define current product model object.
Deprecated: This Property has been deprecated tc12.3 onwards. Please use Cfg0AbsModel::cfg0characteristics instead.
Specifies the Summary Models which summaries the Product Model.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsProductModelFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamily. It represents a family for the product model Features.
The Cfg0AbsProductModelThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsProductModel object.

The Cfg0AbsRule is the abstract type of Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSO. It represents a validation constraint for product variant configurations.User can create the rule expressions such as applicability condition which get associated to the rule object. The product configuration is evaluated against all the configurator rules applicable to the product to determine if it is a valid or invalid configuration. A Cfg0AbsRule can be a global rule which is applicable to all products or it can be a rule specific to one or more products. The Cfg0AbsRule helps user to know the individual expressions set on the rule as well as the complete text representation of the rule.

TcProperty.description: This is an expression indicating that the current rule object is applicable only when this expression is satisfied. For example, for a default rule which should be applied only when V4 Engine for the Car is selected, the applicability condition reads like Engine=V4.
This is a text representation of rule statement.
Represents the suggestive or restrictive clause of the rule. For example, for a default rule which sets Transmission as Manual for the Car, the subject condition reads like Transmission=Manual.

cfg0ExpScript is a runtime property of type string which represents rule object expression as per industry standard. This property is relevant only if cfg0ExpFormat property is Script. For script based rule object, only cfg0ExpScript property will be set and cfg0ApplicabilityCondition and cfg0SubjectCondition should be empty or null.

Runtime property represents the list of intents from families which are used in the expressions of constraint. The default value is NULL. Allowed values are defined in the LOV Cfg0ObjectIntentions. Intents can be any combination of the allowed values in LOV.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsRuleThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelScopedWSOThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsRule object.
The Cfg0AbsSumModelFamilyThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsSummaryModelFamily object.

TcProperty.description: This property is deprecated Teamcenter 10.1.3 onwards and will be removed in Teamcenter 11.1. Please do not use this property.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsSummaryFamilyThread is the abstract thread type of Cfg0AbsCompoundFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionFamily object.

The Cfg0AbsSummaryModel is the abstract type for a Cfg0AbsModel. It defines a group of product models with a common engineering strategy.The Cfg0AbsSummaryModel can be used in constraint rules and/or variant conditions to enforce a consistent relationship with technology options and solutions across all product models represented by this summary model. For example, to group all of its Car models which use Petrol as fuel for example, LXI, VXI, user can create the summary model feature as PetrolModels and make the models LXI and VXI as its members.

TcProperty.description: Specifies the list of model revisions which are summarized by current summary model object.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsSummaryModelFamily is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelFamily. It serves as familiy for summary model Features.
The Cfg0AbsSummaryModelThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsModelThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsSummaryModel object.
The Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionFamily is the abstract type for a Cfg0AbsCompoundValueFamily. It serves as a family for Feature Summaries.

The Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionValue is the abstract type of Cfg0AbsCompoundOptionValue. It represents a set variant configuration options with a common engineering strategy.The Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionValue helps user to group Features with a common engineering strategy. For example, for the product Car, to group Petrol Engines having Engine Features like V4X and V6X, user can create a Petrol Engines Feature Summary as Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionValue with options V4X and V6X as summarized members. The feature summary Petrol Engines function as additional constraint like 'V4X OR V6X' during the product configuration validation. It gives validation error if the feature summary constraint is not met.
The Cfg0AbsSummaryValueThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsCompoundValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionValue object.

The Cfg0AbsValidationRule is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConstraintRule. It defines a configurator constraint rule for validation of product configurations.The Cfg0AbsValidationRule helps user to express an invalid or a feasible combination of Features in a product configuration.
The Cfg0AbsValidationRuleThread is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConstraintRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsValidationRule object.

The Cfg0AbsValue is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO. It represents a product variant configuration Feature.The Cfg0AbsValue represents a unique combination of feature id, family id, and family namespace. It is used to author pre-defined values in a family and it is only relevant for non-free-form families.

TcProperty.description: This property specifies the revision of the Cfg0AbsFamily to which the current Cfg0AbsValue is attached to.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0AbsValueAvailability is the abstract subtype of Cfg0AbsAvailability. It associates the product configuration values with a context object such as Cfg0AbsModel.The Cfg0AbsValueAvailability helps user to make a feature available or un-available to say a Cfg0AbsModel. For example, in Car product with models LXI and ZXI, there could be a Feature 'Rear Wiper' available to only ZXI. This constraint can be materialized using the Cfg0AbsValueAvailability object. The target of the Cfg0AbsValueAvailability will be the Feature 'Rear Wiper' and the context will be the model ZXI. The availability objects behave as constraints during validation of the product configurations.

This attribute holds reference of Cfg0AbsFamilyThread which represents the family for the current Cfg0AbsValueThread.This attribute will facilitate computation of cfg0Family property of Cfg0AbsValue. This is an optional property and can be set as NULL.

The Cfg0AbstractSet helps user to group the variant configuration information for authoring the variant expressions which share a common purpose. It enables authoring and managing a set of related objects together. The objects of this class are not revision configurable. The object_name property of this class is unique, and user can attach naming rule to it.

The Cfg0Allocation is a concrete type of Cfg0AbsAllocation. It associates product configuration data such as Family or feature to a Cfg0ConfContext Item.The Cfg0Allocation helps user to define the owning Cfg0ConfContext Item for product configuration data. It also helps to reuse the same product configurator Family or feature across multiple products. For example, a variant option Coolant can be used in a Refrigerator product as well as in an Air Conditioner product. Hence, user can create the Coolant option and an allocation of the family with a Cfg0Dictionary. The Coolant option acts as the target object of the allocation. User can then create allocations of the same Coolant option with the Refrigerator and Air Conditioner products. In user interface, for a given Cfg0ConfContext Item, a product configurator option object is configured its Cfg0Allocation object is configured in.The Cfg0Allocation object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0Allocation.
The Cfg0AllocationThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsAllocationThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0Allocation object.

The Cfg0AppVariantCriteriaExpr is a subtype of Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp. It stores the variant expression set on a VariantRule object in the grid form. The Cfg0AppVariantCriteriaExpr stores the variant rule criteria expression in grid form and the solve type authored. The details of grid format can be found in description of Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp. As the variant rule criteria expression has a single expression type, the Cfg0AppVariantCriteriaExpr holds single Cfg0VariantExpressionSet and single Cfg0VariantExpSection object. For example, the variant criteria Color=Red and Size=Large will have following grid structure:Cfg0AppVariantCriteriaExpr -> Cfg0VariantExpressionSet -> Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression -> ( Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup -> Cfg0VariantExpressionTerm : (cfg0Operator = PS_variant_operator_is_equal, cfg0ValueText = Red, cfg0FamilyObject = Color object, cfg0ValueObject = Red object) ),( Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup -> Cfg0VariantExpressionTerm : (cfg0Operator = PS_variant_operator_is_equal, cfg0ValueText = Large, cfg0FamilyObject = Size object, cfg0ValueObject = Large object) ).

This class stores the variant expression authored in the grid form. Each section in the variant expression, such as applicability, model condition, etc. is deconstructed in sets (representing columns) and the corresponding sections. This class serves as container to hold the sets and their sections. As it is subclass of Fnd0VariantExpression, it also stores the CNF and string or formula representations of the grid expression. The grid expressions, i.e. set and the tree below it, are constructed only for the variant expressions which are intended to be shown in grid form. The optimized expressions, such as enforced condition, will store the grid form of the variant expression.
The Cfg0ArithmeticConstThread is the instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsArithmeticConstThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ArithmeticConstraint object.

The Cfg0ArithmeticConstraint is instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsArithmeticConstraint. It defines Configurator Constraint to support incremental multiple mathematical operations like += and -= as part of Solve process. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ArithmeticConstraint.

It defines a configurator constraint rule to assert the availability of a Feature against a combination of Features in a product configuration. The applicability of all availability rules for the same subject must be satisfied.
The Cfg0AvailabilityRuleThrd is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsAvailabilityRuleThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AvailabilityRule object.
The CfgAvailabilityThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsAvailabilityThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0Availability object.

Cfg0CombinationRelation is a subtype of IMAN_relation. This business object is created to maintain the relation between Cfg0CombinationTable and Cfg0TableDataset business objects. This relation is used for Combination table constraint in configurator context.

The Cfg0CombinationTable is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsCombinationTable, designed to manage large sets of feature combinations within complex product configurations. This business object enables explicit definition of whether listed combinations represent valid or invalid configurations, ensuring clarity during constraint evaluation. It references a single dataset attachment containing these combinations, supporting scalability for datasets exceeding 20,000 entries. The object enforces data integrity through validation mechanisms and synchronizes changes via timestamp updates, providing robust behavior definition and efficient handling of high-volume configuration data.
The Cfg0CombinationTableThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsCombinationTableThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0CombinationTable object.

Cfg0ConfContext is the abstract subtype of Item. It serves as an anchor object which holds configuration data such as variant options and constraint rules.User can associate variant configuration data with a Cfg0ConfContext Item. User can then associate the Cfg0ConfContext with the product content data such as CollaborativeDesign to consume the configuration data in product content parts in terms of variant conditions and rules.

TcProperty.description: This property will provide the Configurator Perspective instance for the given Configurator Context with default Revision Rule and calculated rule date offset set on it.

TcStandardType.description: Configurator Context
Configurator Context Revision
Configurator Context Revision

The Cfg0ConfigCriteriaEntry stores the a key/value pair of product configuration parameters of a Configurator Criteria object. When user saves a Configurator Criteria, the product configuration parameters such as severity threshold, order or overlay mode, validity and completeness of the configuration are stored as distinct Configurator Criteria Entries.

This business object holds the key information for the Configurator Criteria Entry such as key name, type of value and whether the key can have multiple values. Each Configurator Criteria Key represents a specific instance of a product configuration parameter. The definition of a key and its characteristics are managed in the Product Configurator Application.
The Cfg0ConfiguratorCriteriaThread is a concrete type of Cfg0AbsConfigCriteriaThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ConfiguratorCriteria object.
The Cfg0AbsConfigurationModule is the subtype of Cfg0AbsConfigModuleThread. It represents a thread type which is common to all revisions of a Cfg0AbsConfigurationModule object.

The Cfg0ConfigurationModule is the persistent subtype of Cfg0AbsConfigurationModule. Configurator Module represents a link between a parent configurator context with its child context. Here the parent configurator context remains constant whereas Child context can change for each revision. Using Configuration Module objects, a hierarchy of products can be linked that can evolve independently.

This is deprecated and not used in version 11.5 and above. The Cfg0ConfiguratorCriteria is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsConfiguratorCriteria which stores the product configuration created in Product Configurator Application.

The Cfg0ConstraintSet helps user to group the variant configuration information for authoring the variant expressions which share a common purpose. It enable authoring and managing a set of related constraints together. A constraint can be member of more than one Constraint Set to manage different aspects of same configuration information. The objects of this class are not revision configurable.

The Cfg0DefaultRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsDefaultRule. It defines a configurator rule for defining a default Feature for a combination of Features in a product configuration.The Cfg0DefaultRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0DefaultRule.
The Cfg0DefaultRuleThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsDefaultRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0DefaultRule object.

The Cfg0Dictionary is a concrete subtype of Cfg0ConfContext. It is a configurator context that does not represent a configurable product. Its variant options and rules may apply to multiple, all, or no product.User can create a Cfg0Dictionary and associates common configuration data with it which are applicable to multiple products. For example, a variant option Coolant can be used in a Refrigerator product as well as in an Air Conditioner product. Hence, user can create and associate the Coolant option with a Cfg0Dictionary. User can then associate the Coolant option to the Refrigerator and Air Conditioner products from the Cfg0Dictionary. Similarly, the constraint rules which are applicable to any product (also called as Global Rules) are associated with Cfg0Dictionary. Cfg0Dictionary does not anchor any product specific data such as product models. User can associate the Cfg0Dictionary to product content data such as CollaborativeDesign to consume the configuration data in product content parts in terms of variant conditions and rules.Cfg0Dictionary is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0Dictionary.
Configuration Dictionary
Configuration Dictionary Revision
Configuration Dictionary Revision

The Cfg0EffFamilyThread is the concrete instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsEffFamilyThread. The Cfg0EffFamilyThread is created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0EffFamilyThread. Cfg0EffFamilyThread is not shared as major revision for Effectivity Family is restricted.

The Cfg0EffIntentThread is the concrete instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsEffIntentThread. The Cfg0EffIntentThread is created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0EffIntentThread . Cfg0EffIntentThread is associated to Cfg0EffFanilyThread via cfg0FamilyThread property. Cfg0EffIntentThread is not shared as major revision for Cfg0EffectivityIntent is restricted.

The Cfg0EffectivityExprBlock is a subtype Fnd0EffectivityExprBlock.The Cfg0EffectivityExprBlock is specific to Teamcenter Configurator objects. It can be used to enable POM Revision for the expression blocks associated with Teamcenter configurator objects without affecting the data model of other effectivity configurable object types.

The Cfg0EffectivityFamily is the concrete instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsEffectivityFamily. It serves as family of Effectivity Intent. The Cfg0EffectivityFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot create a subtype or a major revision of Effectivity Family.

The Cfg0EffectivityIntent is the concrete instantiable subtype of Cfg0AbsEffectivityIntent. The Cfg0EffectivityIntent is created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot create a subtype of Effectivity Intent. Cfg0EffectivityIntent knows its associated Effectivity Family via cfg0Family property. Major revision is restricted for Cfg0EffectivityIntent.
The Cfg0ExceptionRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExceptionRule. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ExceptionRule object. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ExceptionRule.

The Cfg0ExceptionRuleThrd is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExceptionRuleThrd. The Cfg0ExceptionRuleThrd is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ExceptionRuleThrd.

The Cfg0ExcludeRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExcludeRule. It defines an incompatibility of a Feature for a combination of Features in a product configuration.The Cfg0ExcludeRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ExcludeRule.
The Cfg0ExcludeRuleThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExcludeRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ExcludeRule object.
Cfg0ExternalOperBlockThread is the business object and a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExternalOperBlockThd which represents external operation thread in Product Configurator
Cfg0ExternalOperation is the business object and a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExternalOperation which represents external operation in Product Configurator
Cfg0ExternalOperationBlock is the business object and a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExternalOperBlock which represents external operations block in Product Configurator
Cfg0ExternalOperationThread is the business object and a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsExternalOperThread which represents external operation thread in Product Configurator

The Cfg0FamilyAvailability is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFamilyAvailability. It makes a product configuration object like Cfg0AbsFamily available to a context object like Cfg0AbsModel.The Cfg0FamilyAvailability objects are created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot subtype the Cfg0FamilyAvailability.

The Cfg0FamilyGroup is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup. It acts as a container of variant configuration families of type Cfg0AbsFamily.The Cfg0FamilyGroup is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FamilyGroup.
The Cfg0FamilyGroupThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFamilyGroupThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FamilyGroup object.

The Cfg0FeasibilityRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeasibilityRule. It defines a configurator constraint rule to assert the feasibility of a Feature against a combination of Features in a product configuration.The Cfg0FeasibilityRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FeasibilityRule.
The Cfg0FeasibilityRuleThrd is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeasibilityRuleThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FeasibilityRule object.
The Cfg0Feature is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeature. The Cfg0Feature is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0Feature.

The Cfg0FeatureFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily. The Cfg0FeatureFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FeatureFamily.
The Cfg0FeatureFamilyThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeatureFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FeatureFamily object.
The Cfg0FeatureSet is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeatureSet. The Cfg0FeatureSet is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FeatureSet.
The Cfg0FeatureSetThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeatureSetThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FeatureSet object.
The Cfg0FeatureThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFeatureThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FeatureThread object. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FeatureThread.

The Cfg0FreeFormRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFreeFormRule. It defines a configurator constraint rule for dependency of Features in a product configuration. The Cfg0FreeFormRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FreeFormRule.
The Cfg0FreeFormRuleThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsFreeFormRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0FreeFormRule object. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0FreeFormRuleThread.

The Cfg0IncludeRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsIncludeRule. It defines a configurator constraint rule for dependency of Features in a product configuration.The Cfg0IncludeRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0IncludeRule.
The Cfg0IncludeRuleThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsIncludeRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0IncludeRule object.
The Cfg0LiteralFamilyThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsLiteralFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0LiteralValueFamily object.

The Cfg0LiteralOptionValue is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsLiteralOptionValue. It represents the non-compound and non-model variant configuration options.The Cfg0LiteralOptionValue is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0LiteralOptionValue.

The Cfg0LiteralValueFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsLiteralValueFamily. It serves as family of the non-compound and non-model variant configuration values.The Cfg0LiteralValueFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0LiteralValueFamily.
The Cfg0LiteralValueThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsLiteralValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0LiteralOptionValue object.

The Cfg0MatrixRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsMatrixRule. It defines a configurator constraint for dependency of features for a base variant in a product configuration. The Cfg0MatrixRule object is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0MatrixRule.
The Cfg0MatrixRuleThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsMatrixRuleThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0MatrixRule object.

The Cfg0OptionValueAvailability is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsValueAvailability. It makes a product configuration feature available to a context object such as Cfg0AbsModel.The Cfg0OptionValueAvailability objects are created and managed in Product Configurator application. User cannot create a subtype for Cfg0OptionValueAvailability.
The Cfg0PackageFamilyThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0PackageOptionFamily object.

The Cfg0PackageOptionFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageOptionFamily. It serves as family for Feature Packages.The Cfg0PackageOptionFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0PackageOptionFamily.

The Cfg0PackageOptionValue is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageOptionValue. It represents compound variant configuration options such as Feature Packages.The Cfg0PackageOptionValue is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0PackageOptionValue.
The Cfg0PackageRule is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageRule. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0PackageRule object. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0PackageRule.
The Cfg0PackageRuleThrd is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageRuleThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0PackageRule object. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0PackageRuleThrd.
The Cfg0PackageValueThread is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsPackageValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0PackageOptionValue object.
The Cfg0ProdModelFamilyThread is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProdModelFamilyThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ProductModelFamily object.

The Cfg0ProductItem is a concrete subtype of Cfg0ConfContext. It is a configurator context that manages variant options and rules for a specific configurable product.User can create a Cfg0ProductItem and associate the product specific configuration data to it. For example, variant option DoorType such as 3-Door, 2-Door can be used only in a Refrigerator product and not in Air Conditioner product. Hence, user can create and associate the DoorType option on a Cfg0ProductItem for Refrigerator product. Similarly, the constraint rules which are applicable to specific product are associated with Cfg0ProductItem. The product models are always specific to a product and hence, Cfg0ProductItem also anchors the product models. User can associate the Cfg0ProductItem to product content data such as CollaborativeDesign to consume the configuration data in product content parts in terms of variant conditions and rules.Cfg0ProductItem is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ProductItem.
Configuration Product Context
Configuration Product Context Revision
Configuration Product Context Revision

The Cfg0ProductLine is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductLine. It represents Features to provide the product line variant configurations to user.The Cfg0ProductLine is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ProductLine.
The Cfg0ProductLineFamThrd is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductLineFamThrd. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ProductLineFamily object.

The Cfg0ProductLineFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductLineFamily. It serves family for the product line Features.The Cfg0ProductLineFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create subtype of Cfg0ProductLineFamily.
The Cfg0ProductLineThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductLineThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ProductLine object.

The Cfg0ProductModel is the concrete type of Cfg0AbsProductModel. It represents the product model Features.The Cfg0ProductModel is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ProductModel.

The Cfg0ProductModelFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductModelFamily. It serves as family for model Features.The Cfg0ProductModelFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0ProductModelFamily.
The Cfg0ProductModelThread is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsProductModelThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0ProductModel object.

DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. The Cfg0RangeExpression is part of the variant expression in the grid form and stored in a Cfg0VariantExpressionTerm object.The Cfg0RangeExpression contains a value range expression. For example, the expression set on an object is a range like length = 10..20, then the Cfg0VariantExpressionTerm will contain two Cfg0RangeExpression objects. One for a range expression of length >=10 and other for length <= 20. The grid structure looks like:Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp -> Cfg0VariantExpressionSet -> ( Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression -> Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup -> Cfg0VariantExpressionTerm : (cfg0FamilyObject = length object, (Cfg0RangeExpression : (cfg0Operator = PS_variant_operator_gt_eq, cfg0ValueText = 10 ), (Cfg0RangeExpression : (cfg0Operator = PS_variant_operator_lt_eq, cfg0ValueText = 20 )))).
The Cfg0SumModelFamilyThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSumModelFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0SummaryModelFamily object.
The Cfg0SummaryFamilyThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryFamilyThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0SummaryOptionFamily object.

The Cfg0SummaryModel is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryModel. It defines a group of product models with a common engineering strategy.The Cfg0SummaryModel is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0SummaryModel.

The Cfg0SummaryModelFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryModelFamily. It serves as a family for summary model values.The Cfg0SummaryModelFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0SummaryModelFamily.
The Cfg0SummaryModelThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryModelThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0SummaryModel object.

The Cfg0SummaryOptionFamily is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionFamily. It serves as family for Feature Summaries.The Cfg0SummaryOptionFamily is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype a Cfg0SummaryOptionFamily.

The Cfg0SummaryOptionValue is the concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryOptionValue. It represents a set variant configuration options with a common engineering strategy.The Cfg0SummaryOptionValue is created and managed in Product Configurator Application. User cannot create a subtype of Cfg0SummaryOptionValue.
The Cfg0AbsSummaryValueThread is a concrete subtype of Cfg0AbsSummaryValueThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0SummaryOptionValue object.

The Cfg0VariantCriteria is the subtype of VariantRule which stores the product configuration information like Variant Expression, Revision Rule, Effectivity, RuleDate, Order/Overlay Mode, IsValid, IsComplete etc. This configuration information is stored as collection of Key/Value Pairs. User creates a Variant Criteria to persist a product configuration created in Product Configurator Application to retrieve and apply to product content.

The Cfg0VariantCriteriaBlock is a subtype of Fnd0VariantExprBlock. It stores the Product Configurator session information along with the variant expressions. The Cfg0VariantCriteriaBlock is created and managed in Product Configurator with the help of VariantConfigurable and ConfigurationSession behaviors.

TcProperty.description: Property cfg0Features is an array of TypedReference which represents the list of the configured features. Property Features will list all the configured revisions of Cfg0AbsValueThread and Cfg0AbsFeatureThread objects from the persisted property fnd0ImpactingObjects. fnd0ImpactingObjects which are thread objects, need to go through revision configuration to get its associated Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO. Property Features will help users filter on the Solution Variants based on the features. NULL value is allowed, it would mean there are no configured Features available for this configuration.

TcStandardType.description: The Cfg0VariantCriteriaThread is a subtype of Fnd0WSOThread. It is common to all revisions of a Cfg0VariantRule object. It holds a unique identifier for the Cfg0VariantCriteria.

DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. The Cfg0VariantExpSection is part of the variant expression in the grid form and stored in a Cfg0VariantExpressionSet object.The Cfg0VariantExpSection contains ORed combination of sub-expression. For an Cfg0ExcludeRule with model condition is Model=Economy, applicability is Fuel Type=Petrol and payload is Transmission=Auto, the grid structure will have three Cfg0VariantExpSection objects corresponding to model, applicability and payload. Each Cfg0VariantExpSection contains single sub-expression :Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp -> Cfg0VariantExpressionSet -> Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression : Model=Economy, Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression : Fuel Type=Petrol, Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression : Transmission=Auto.The next level of details for above grid structure will be found in description of Cfg0VariantSubExpression.This class also stores the CNF and string or formula representations of the variant expression. This information is used during constraint evaluation against product configuration.

The Cfg0VariantExprBlock is a subtype Fnd0VariantExprBlock.The Cfg0VariantExprBlock is specific to Teamcenter Configurator objects. It can be used to enable POM Revision for the expression blocks associated with Teamcenter Configurator objects without affecting the data model of other variant configurable object types.

DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. Contains a set of expression terms. A mixture of positive and negated expression terms in the same group is not allowed. Positive terms are combined with operator OR. Negated terms are combined with operator AND.

DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. The Cfg0VariantExpressionSet is part of the variant expression in the grid form and stored in a Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp object.The Cfg0VariantExpressionSet contains ANDed combination of expression sections. For an Cfg0ExcludeRule with model condition as Model=Economy, applicability as Fuel Type=Petrol and payload as Transmission=Auto, the grid structure will have single Cfg0VariantExpressionSet with three Cfg0VariantExpSection objects :Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp -> Cfg0VariantExpressionSet -> Cfg0VariantExpSection : Model=Economy, Cfg0VariantExpSection : Fuel Type=Petrol, Cfg0VariantExpSection : Transmission=Auto.The next level of details for above grid structure will be found in description of Cfg0VariantExpSection.
DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. Represents an expression literal or a value range expression.

DEPRECATED. SEE SUPPORT ANNOUNCEMENT 2606. The Cfg0VariantSubExpression is part of the variant expression in the grid form and stored in a Cfg0VariantExpSection object.The Cfg0VariantSubExpression contains ANDed combination of expression groups. For a Cfg0ExcludeRule with model condition as Model=Economy, applicability as Fuel Type=Petrol and payload as Transmission=Auto, the grid structure will have three Cfg0VariantSubExpression, each one in corresponding Cfg0VariantExpSection. Each Cfg0VariantSubExpression contains one Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup :Cfg0ApplicationVariantExp -> Cfg0VariantExpressionSet -> ( Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression -> Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup : Model=Economy ), ( Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression -> Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup : Fuel Type=Petrol ), ( Cfg0VariantExpSection -> Cfg0VariantSubExpression -> Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup : Transmission=Auto ).The next level of details for above grid structure will be found in description of Cfg0VariantExpressionGroup.

TcProperty.description: Returns the runtime Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective object.
Specifies a Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective object which represents the collection of product configuration parameters retrieved from Configurator Variant Rule. This is a read only property.
Retrieves Solve Profile information present on Variant Rule

Runtime property stores list of object intents. The default value is NULL. The property is stored as a solve profile key in Cfg0VariantCriteriaBlock, which is referenced in VariantRule. Allowed values are defined in the LOV Cfg0ObjectIntentions. Intents can be any combination of the allowed values.

This is a Boolean property that indicates if the criteria expression is complete when saving a Variant object. If the SVR is complete, it will be saved with "TRUE". If the SVR is completable but not complete it must have been expanded before saving to be saved with "TRUE". If the SVR was expanded before saving but turned out to be incomplete it will be saved with "FALSE". Otherwise, it will be saved with "NULL".
This is a Boolean property that indicates if the criteria expression is valid with respect to product configurator constraints when saving a Variant object. A NULL or empty value means unknown.

This date property shows the date and time when we last validated or Expanded the current Variant object. This property helps us understand if we need to re-validate or re-expand the Variant object due to changes in Configurator Variability and update the object with properties like 'cfg0IsValid' and 'cfg0IsComplete'. Here dates are localized based on text server key "DefaultDateFormat" in timelocal_locale.xml.

This property indicates the depth of the product hierarchy for the current configuration. Valid values are 1, 2, 3, and 4. Users can use CFG0_get_configuration_information ITK to extract a perspective where "VariantRule::cfg0ProductHierarchyDepth" and "Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective::cfg0ProductHierarchyDepth" return the same values. To get Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective of VariantRule, users can use AOM_ask_value_tag(VariantRule, "cfg0ConfigPerspective", &Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective).

This property displays the Revision Rule name as per the time of creation of current configuration. Users can use CFG0_get_configuration_information ITK to extract a perspective where "VariantRule::cfg0RevisionRule" represent name of Revision Rule object from property "Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective::cfg0RevisionRule". To get Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective of VariantRule, users can use AOM_ask_value_tag(VariantRule, "cfg0ConfigPerspective", &Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective).

This property displays the configuration date translation policy of the current configuration. This string can be 'System Default', 'Latest', 'No Rule Date' or 'Date' stored in criteria key "CFG_PROFILE_ruleDateTranslation" of Variant Rule.

This property displays the Rule Date as per the time of creation of current configuration. Users can use CFG0_get_configuration_information ITK to extract a perspective where "VariantRule::cfg0RuleSetCompiledDate" and "Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective::cfg0RuleSetCompiledDate" match up. To get Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective of VariantRule, users can use AOM_ask_value_tag(VariantRule, "cfg0ConfigPerspective", &Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective). Here dates are localized based on text server key "DefaultDateFormat" in timelocal_locale.xml.

This property shows the "effectivity" as a Teamcenter formula for the current configuration. Users can use CFG0_get_configuration_information ITK to extract a perspective where "VariantRule::cfg0RuleSetEffectivity" and "Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective::cfg0RuleSetEffectivity" match up. To get Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective of VariantRule, users can use AOM_ask_value_tag(VariantRule, "cfg0ConfigPerspective", &Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective).

This property shows the solve profile information for the current configuration as a string. It includes profile names defined by the Teamcenter preference 'PCA_solver_profiles'. This property reflects the name as it existed at the time of saving the SVR. If the profile name or its definition have changed since the SVR was saved, the Variant Rule property will be out of sync. Users can select any existing solve profile when creating a Variant or its subtypes. If no profile is specified, the system shows the first profile set by 'PCA_solver_profiles' on Variant Rule.
Expression indicating the criteria for content to configure. For example, when V4 Engine for the Car is selected, the condition reads like "Engine=V4".
Returns the localized text representation of variant expression set on the VariantRule object.

TcGlobalConstant.description: Business Constant to allow user to configure list objects types to be exempted from availability check. Object types mentioned and its subtype objects are exempted. Only object types name are allowed in this constant except text "FreeFormFamily". "FreeFormFamily" is the only non-object string to exempt values of Option Family which are characterized as free form family. If administrator changes the value of constant, they have to delete all instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet. To delete instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet, administrator will follow below steps. 1. Login with 'infodba' user. 2. Search the all instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet using My Teamcenter. 3. Select all search result and delete them using Delete action.
TcGlobalConstant.name: Cfg0ExemptAvailabilityChecks

TcGlobalConstant.description:
Specifies if Configurator's primary business relevant attribute is Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.cfg0ObjectId or Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.object_name in the Product Configurator application. Valid values are "Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.object_name" or "Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.cfg0ObjectId". Any value other than these two values or empty value or absence of global constant is treated as Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.cfg0ObjectId. Display formula string will use the global constant value. If constant value is Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.object_name then display formula will contain object_name else it will contain cfg0ObjectId. Teamcenter RAC client views and runtime properties on Business Object honor value of the global constant to display the formula strings. Value specified in this global constant is case sensitive. The value of DisplayName business object constant for configurator business objects should be in sync with the value of primary business relevant attribute. For instance, if the value of primary business relevant attribute is Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO.object_name, then DisplayName constant for configurator business objects should have value $object_name. Use Case: ID Name Type 1[NS] - Size - Integer | |__38 - Small |__40 - Medium
3[NS] - Color - String | |__#0000FF - Blue |__#008000 - Green
19[NS] - Full Sleeve - Boolean |__19 - Yes
24[NS] - Milestone Dates - Date |__31-Jul-2018 - Release Date |__31-May-2018 - Freeze Date
Display formula with cfg0ObjectId Subject: ([Teamcenter]3 = #0000FF)
Applicablity: ([Teamcenter]19 = true AND [Teamcenter]1 = 40 AND [Teamcenter]21 = '31-May-2018 00:00')
Display formula with object_name: Subject: ([Teamcenter]Color = Blue)
Applicablity: ([Teamcenter]'Full Sleeve' = true AND [Teamcenter]Size = Medium AND [Teamcenter]'Milestone Dates' = 'Freeze Date')
TcGlobalConstant.name: Cfg0PrimaryBusinessRelevantAttribute

TcTypeConstant.description: The Cfg0AllocationType constant serves as a mechanism for managing allocation types for Cfg0AbsFamily, Cfg0AbsValue Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup and their subtypes. Its primary purpose is to define and control allocation type across different configurator objects. The default value is set to "Cfg0Allocation". Users should ensure that all subtypes supporting allocation update their allocation type appropriately, strictly adhering to the requirement that values must be subtypes of Cfg0AbsAllocation. The constant should be used when creating new configurator WSO subtypes requiring allocation support or implementing custom allocation behavior. As an alternative, users can consider using composition instead of inheritance by customizing "Cfg0Allocation" through composition.
TcTypeConstant.name: Cfg0AllocationType

TcTypeConstant.description: The type of Feature to be used by family objects. Default value is empty. All instantiable types must update valid thread type for respective revision type. It is recommended that abstract classes do not mention any value for this business type constant.
TcTypeConstant.name: Cfg0DefaultValueType

TcTypeConstant.description: Setting this constant to true enables EffectivityConfigurable behavior. If no effectivity condition was saved for the object it passes Effectivity filters only when a solve type is used that includes bit pattern 128 or the equivalent for the inverse solve type (see preference TC_default_Solve_Type). A value of false disables EffectivityConfigurable behavior. The object passes Effectivity filters only when a solve type is used that includes bit pattern 256.
TcTypeConstant.name: Cfg0EnableEffectivityConfigurableBehavior

TcTypeConstant.description: Business Constant to allow administrator to configure the Cfg0AbsRule types to behavior for Bidirectional. The type of this constant is Boolean. True value represents Rules behavior as bidirectional else behave like unidirectional. The value of constant is applicable to subtypes of Business objects else it is overridden. If the Cfg0IsBidirectional is set as true it means the following: a. Cfg0AbsIncludeRule: The rule becomes an equivalence for example, Applicability Condition == Subject Condition. b. Cfg0AbsPacakgeRule: The rule becomes an equivalence for example, Applicability Condition == Subject Condition. c. Cfg0AbsExcludeRule: The rule becomes an XOR for example, Applicability Condition ^ Subject Condition. This Business constant is not applicable for Cfg0AbsDefaultRule and Cfg0AbsAvailabilityRule. If administrator changes the value of constant, they have to delete all instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet. To delete instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet, administrator will follow below steps. 1. Login with infodba user. 2. Search the all instances of Cfg0CompiledRuleSet using My Teamcenter. 3. Select all search result and delete them using Delete action.
TcTypeConstant.name: Cfg0IsBidirectional

TcTypeConstant.description: The type of thread used by objects of instantiable revision types should be exact or subtype of given thread type. Default value is empty. All instantiable types must update valid thread type for respective revision type. It is recommended that abstract classes do not mention any value for this business type constant.
TcTypeConstant.name: Cfg0ThreadType

ServiceInterface.description:
This Service contains operations related to variant configuration and variant configurator data. The createObjects operation in the DataManagementService can be used to create configurator or variability data such as feature (e.g. Cfg0LiteralOptionValue) and their families. The families can be arranged into family groups (e.g. Cfg0FamilyGroup). The features, families, and family groups need to be allocated to items in order to make them visible to these items.

The configurator rules ( Cfg0AbsRule or subtypes) reference a set of product items and define the relationship among variant option values in the context of these product item(s). The configurator rules can be categorized broadly as the default rules (e.g. Cfg0AbsDefaultRule) and the constraint rules (Cfg0AbsContraintRule). The constraint rule business object types can further be categorized as rule to validate (e.g. Cfg0AbsExcludeRule) and to modify (e.g. Cfg0AbsIncludeRule) the configuration criteria. All constraint rules are imperative in nature, while all default rules are suggestive.

The configuration rules that derive from Cfg0AbsAssociation type define the relationship between the variability data (such as features, families or family groups) and a product configuration context. For example variability data is not visible in a product item until it is explicitly allocated to this product (e.g. with a Cfg0Allocation object). For product context items with positive biased variant availability (see Item property fnd0PosBiasedVariantAvail) all variability data is available by default. In this case explicit availability rules (e.g.Cfg0ValueAvailability) are only required if the corresponding variability data needs to be made unavailable.

Most of the operations in this service needs the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective) runtime business object as part of the input parameter. Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective is a runtime business object that represents the configuration snapshot required for the Product Configurator in Teamcenter. Since constructing the configurator perspective runtime business object may take time, you should create it first time for a given Configurator context object and hold it for the subsequent calls. Hold the configurator perspective runtime business object for a configurator context if the configuration is unchanged. You always work on a snapshot or a frozen set of the configurator data and use that data to get consistent results for a period. These results are not impacted by subsequent changes, such as additions or updates of features and rules.
Since getting the Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective runtime business object for a configurator context may involve effort by the system in destroying and creating the snapshot, you should get it once for a given configurator context object and hold it as long as the configuration (revision rule, rule date and effectivity) is unchanged.
The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective runtime object is a session recoverable object which means that the system will try to facilitate transparent recovery of the business object when a TcServer instance crashes.
The sample in soa_client.zip, com.teamcenter.productconfigurator.GetConfiguratorPerspectiveSampleTest.java shows the different ways the user can get the Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective runtime object.
ServiceInterface.name: ConfiguratorManagement

Struct.description:
The structure represents response for the getAvailableVariability operation consisting of available variability for the requested families, expanded expression, status of the configuration and a service data.
To get the details of violations for invalid configuration or list of families with missing selections for valid and incomplete configuration, the validateAndExpandExpressions service operation should be called.
Struct.name: AvailableVariabilityResponse

StructElement.description: A list of available variability for the families of interest. An entry in the list contains a requested family along with its available features or range expressions. The size of the list is same as number of input families and sequence will match with the input families’ sequence. An input family with no valid values will contain an element of available variability with zero expression terms. The list will be empty in case of invalid configuration.
StructElement.name: availableVariability

StructElement.description: The expanded expression satisfying the given input expression and set of constraint(s) for the given configurator context. It will consist of input expression along with system suggested features only for the requested families. The expanded expression will be present in the response only for a valid configuration.
StructElement.name: expandedExpression

StructElement.description: True if the configuration is valid. To know the violations for an invalid configuration, the validateAndExpandExpressions operation should be called.
StructElement.name: isValid

StructElement.description:
The completeness status of the configuration. If the configuration is valid then the completeness status values can either be Complete or Incomplete.
Valid values are as follows:
•    0 – Unknown; When the configuration is invalid, the completeness is unknown.
•    1 – Incomplete; not all families in the configuration have value selections. getAvailableVariability operation does not provide the list of missing families as it is expanded only in input families scope. To know the list of missing families, the system needs to expand in full family scope. Use validateAndExpandExpressions service operation to know the list of all families missing selections for incomplete configuration.
•    2 – Complete; all families in the configuration have value selections.
StructElement.name: isComplete

Users can request the validation against the unoptimized ruleset to get violations with unmodified constraints.

Family (Cfg0AbsOptionFamily) or Feature Family (Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily) business object revision represented by the structure.

For a Family revision to be returned as part of the operation’s response, it must satisfy the following requirements:

•    Configured Revision: The Revision Rule in the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0RevisionRule) must select a valid family revision (Cfg0AbsOptionFamily and Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily) and family allocation revision (Cfg0AbsAllocation).
•    Product Allocation: The “Configurator Contexts” property of the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0ProductItems) must match the “Configurator Context” property of the revision rule configured Family allocation revision (Cfg0AbsAllocation.cfg0ProductItem).

Standalone Features (Cfg0AbsFeature) must be a member of the current Feature Family (Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily).

StructElement.description:
The group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup ) business object represented by the structure. This object identifies the navigation structure in in Guided Variant Configuration (active validation). The following characteristics are important in this context:
1.    Family Groups (and Family Group allocations) cannot be revised.
2.    The same Family Group may be allocated to multiple Configurator Contexts.
3.    Family Groups may contain families across multiple products.
4.    Allocating a Family Group does not automatically allocate its families. Configurator Contexts may choose to only allocate a subset of the families in each Family Group.
StructElement.name: famGroup

StructElement.description:
The allocation object (Cfg0AbsAssociation) with respect to the current object and input configurator context.
The “Configurator Contexts” property of the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0ProductItems) must match a Family Group allocation revision with read access.
The Family Group allocation revision is not subject to revision rule configuration.

StructElement.description:
Feature and Standalone Feature (Cfg0AbsOptionValue and Cfg0AbsFeature) which are attached to the current family. It is of type Cfg0AbsConfiguratorWSO (common parent) as it may hold either Cfg0AbsOptionValue or Cfg0AbsFeature type.
If it is of type Standalone Feature (Cfg0AbsFeature) then it must be a member of Feature Family (Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily.cfg0Features).
The Revision Rule in the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0RevisionRule) must select a valid feature revision.
For a revision of a feature to be configured for the given revision rule, the following objects must also be configured:
    • Feature revision (Cfg0AbsOptionValue and Cfg0AbsFeature)
    • Feature allocation revision (Cfg0AbsAllocation)
    • Family revision (Cfg0AbsOptionFamily and Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily)
    • Family allocation revision (Cfg0AbsAllocation)

The Revision Rule in the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0RevisionRule) must select a valid feature allocation revision. The “Configurator Contexts” property of the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective.cfg0ProductItems) must match the “Configurator Context” property of the revision rule configured feature allocation revision (Cfg0AbsAllocation.cfg0ProductItem).

StructElement.description:
For future use. Currently it will be empty in the response. The filter struct allows user to filter the output response. The filter struct has name and values the server can use to specify what kind of data was requested. It returns the response key-value pairs for the corresponding request key-value pairs.

The valid name-values are

    • Cfg0::response:filter:Groups – Represents a Boolean value. If true, then returns the list of family group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup) objects as part of the GetVariabilityResponse.groups member. Default is true.
    • Cfg0::response:filter::Products – Represents a Boolean value. If true, then returns Product model, Product Line, Summary Models as part of the GetVariablityResponse.productFamilies member. Default is true.
    • Cfg0::response:filter:UngroupedFamilies – Represents a Boolean value. If true, the operation returns the families that are not part of any group as part of the GetVariablityResponse.ungroupedFamilies member. Default is true.

Struct.description: ConfigsBasedOnOptFamilyInput is a structure that defines the inputs required for generating configurations based optimization familiy. It includes a runtime perspective snapshot, a solve profile for constraint evaluation, optional limiting for filtering configurations, bound expressions, a flag to determine optimization direction (maximum or minimum), and a list of valid product families to compute the configurations.

StructElement.description: Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective is a runtime business object representing a snapshot of a Configurator Product Context object. The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.
StructElement.name: perspective

StructElement.description: The configuration solve profile is a JSON string that consists of attributes governing the behavior of the configurator constraint evaluation. This string should adhere to the JSON schema for solve profile defined in SolveProfile_Schema.json ; please refer to schema and sample solve profiles defined at %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema for details. Each solve profile key should occur only once in the solve profile JSON string.
StructElement.name: solveProfile

StructElement.description: A limiting expression which is used to compute the configurations . The Computed output configurations must satisfy this limiting expression. The limiting expression can be empty since it is an optional parameter.
StructElement.name: limitingExpression

StructElement.description: A bound expression defines the optimization scope for the Family, which can be optimized for either a minimum or maximum value based on the optimizeForMaxValue parameter. Bound Expression must be literal expresssion with numeric family. Family contained in boundExpression will be part of the output configurations. For example, if optimizeForMaxValue is true and the optimization family is weight, then setting ‘Weight = 100’ means the maximum allowed weight is ‘100’. If any valid configuration exceeds this limit, the system returns error code CFG_solution_exists_outside_specified_bound_for_max. Conversely, if optimizeForMaxValue is false and the optimization family is weight, then setting ‘Weight = 10’ means the minimum allowed weight is ‘10’. StructElement.description:
The set operator to use when combining the results from each search definition in this group. Possible values are:
    • "UnionAll"
    • "UnionUnique"
    • "Intersection"
    • "Difference"

Use "UnionAll" if search results are not expected to contain duplicates, or if duplicates are not a concern. The search expressions in this group are combined in the sequence in which they appear in the group.

"UnionAll" and "UnionUnique" combine the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. "UnionAll" does not remove duplicates and is therefore often faster.

"Intersection" combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left as well as the right search definition operand.

"Difference" combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left but not from the right search definition operand.

Search definitions constructed from a ResultTypeInput are always combined with "Intersection".

Exclude search definitions constructed from a ObjectReferenceInput are always combined with "Difference".

Include search definitions constructed from a ObjectReferenceInput are combined with "UnionAll" if the set operator for the group is "UnionAll", otherwise with "UnionUnique".

For example, a "UnionAll" group that combines the following search definitions:
    • "savedQuery"
    • "includeObjects"
    • "resultTypes"
    • "excludeObjects"

would return:
$savedQuery UnionAll $includeObjects Intersection $resultTypes Difference $excludeObjects.
StructElement.name: searchOperator

StructElement.description: The list of client Ids of the search expressions to combine in this group. Any client ID that is assigned to a search definition input structure within the same <font face="courier" height="10">SearchExpressionInput</font> can be used, including other <font face="courier" height="10">ExpressionGroupInput</font> client ID values. For example you could specify two client ID values that are given in the "<font face="courier" height="10">savedQueries</font>" parameter of the SearchExpressionInput that also contains this <font face="courier" height="10">ExpressionGroupInput</font> structure if you want to intersect or union the results from these two searches. Or you could combine one of the client ID values in parameter "<font face="courier" height="10">savedQueries</font>" with one of the ID values in parameter "<font face="courier" height="10">excludeObjects</font>" if you want to explicitly remove some objects from the search results of the saved query. This <font face="courier" height="10">ExpressionGroupInput</font> then forms a new search criterion as a combination of the results from the search definitions that are referenced in this list.

MetaEnum.description:
Set operator values to use when combining the results from each search definition in a ExpressionGroupInput.
    • UnionAll     - Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. Duplicates are not removed from the combined set.
    • UnionUnique -    Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains a unique list of objects that includes objects returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. The combined set will not contain duplicates.
    • Intersection -    Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left as well as the right search definition operand.
    • Difference    - Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left but not from the right search definition operand.
MetaEnum.name: SearchGroupOperator

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. Duplicates are not removed from the combined set.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: UnionAll

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains a unique list of objects that includes objects returned from either the left or the right search definition operand. The combined set will not contain duplicates.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: UnionUnique

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left as well as the right search definition operand.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: Intersection

MetaEnumLiteral.description: Combines the results of two search definitions into a set that contains all of the objects that are returned from the left but not from the right search definition operand.
MetaEnumLiteral.name: Difference

MetaEnum.description:
Join operator values to use when combining the results from each search definition in a ExpressionJoinInput.

    • InnerJoin - Combines the column values of two searches (A and B) based upon a join condition. The join compares each row of A with each row of B to find all pairs of rows which satisfy the join condition.
    • LeftJoin - The result of a left join for searches A and B always contains all records of the "left" search (A), even if the join condition does not find any matching record in the "right" search (B).
    • RightJoin - The result of a right join for searches A and B always contains all records of the "right" search (B), even if the join condition doesn't find any matching record in the "left" search (A).
    • FullJoin - The result of a full join for searches A and B always contains all records of both searches. Where records in A and B don't match, the result set will have NULL values for every column of the search that lacks a matching row. For those records that do match, a single row will be produced in the result set (containing fields populated from both searches).
MetaEnum.name: SearchJoinOperator

StructElement.description:
Indicates whether or not to apply the constraints. The parameter value is a bit pattern specifying the requested operation. A parameter value of 25 reports warnings and informational messages in addition to errors :
Apply constraints | Report Warnings | Report Info = 1+8+16 = 25
0 - indicates constraint application is not required
1 - apply configuration constraints
2 - skip constraints if they only reference unset families
4 - skip constraints that don't reference all configExpression families
8 - report warnings in addition to errors
16 - also report informational messages
32 - continue Validation On Error
64 - treat constraints with warning severity as if they had error severity
128 - skip all variability checks which could raise a "k_variant_criteria_outside" validation failure
256 - skip the check against allocated variability which could raise a "k_variant_criteria_outside" validation failure
1024 - skip criteria update based on validation rules ( e.g. Exclude rule ). If this flag is not set it will update the criteria after applying validation rules
2048 - enable Availability Constraint evaluation
StructElement.name: applyConstraints

StructElement.description: This index identifies the input structure for which overlap states are recorded.
StructElement.name: index

StructElement.description:
Each overlap state value indicates the degree of overlap between the expression at a given index in the corresponding input structure and the reference expression in that input structure.
The getDisplayStrings operation in the SessionService can be used to obtain a display value for each of the following overlap state keys:
    • k_overlapstate_none: The two expressions have no overlap. There is no satisfying solution common to both expressions. A conjunction (AND combination) of the two is unsatisfiable.
    • k_overlapstate_subset: The two expressions overlap. The solution set of the expression is a subset of the solution set of the reference expression. The conjunction (AND combination) of the expression with the negated reference expression is unsatisfiable.
    • k_overlapstate_match: The two expressions are logically equivalent. Every solution that satisfies one expression also satisfies the other, and vice versa.
    • k_overlapstate_superset: The two expressions overlap. The solution set of the expression is a superset of the solution set of the reference expression. The conjunction (AND combination) of the negated expression with the reference expression is unsatisfiable.
    • k_overlapstate_intersect: The two expressions overlap. The solution set of the expression has some overlap with the solution set of the reference expression.
StructElement.name: overlapStates
