StructElement.description:
How to apply the constraints. The action is a bitwise OR the following values:
0: disable configurator constraint evaluation
1: enable configurator constraint evaluation
2: skip constraints if they only reference unset families
4: skip constraints that don't reference all configExpression families
8: report warnings in addition to errors
16: report informational messages
32: don't stop if a violation is encountered (use with care)
64: treat constraints with warning severity as if they had error severity.

1024: skip criteria update based on validation rules (For example configurator exclusion rule). If this flag is not set then the operation will update the variant criteria after applying validation rules.

2048: enable Availability Constraint evaluation.
StructElement.name: applyConstraints

StructElement.description:
Specifies the selection type of the feature object. This parameter specifies whether the feature object is user selected, default selected or system selected.

Valid Values are as follow:
    • EmptyInitialized A constraint has initialized a family with the empty value.
    • Default         A constraint has assigned a default value.
    • PackageDefault A package constraint has assigned a default value.
    • Unknown         An administrator authored constraint with unknown severity has assigned a value. If a feature selection is not known precisely, it will be represented as unknown.
    • Information     A constraint with Info severity has assigned a value. Refer Cfg0ConstraintSeverity list of values for details.
    • Warning         A constraint with Warning severity has assigned a value. Refer Cfg0ConstraintSeverity list of values for details.
    • Error            A constraint with Error severity has assigned a value. Refer Cfg0ConstraintSeverity list of values for details.
    • User             User has assigned a value.

StructElement.description:
The default actions to apply. The parameter is a bitwise OR the following values:
    • 0 - Indicates that defaults should not be applied
    • 1 - Will enable application of defaults
    • 2 - Ignore all derived defaults and only process fixed defaults
    • 4 - Skip derived defaults whose applicability or product model condition is not fully and explicitly satisfied. For example, a default rule 'set W=10 if H=10' is skipped for the input expression 'L=10' because 'L=10' also includes configurations that don't satisfy the applicability condition, such as 'L=10 & H=20'.
    • 8 - Force partially satisfied derived defaults.

Struct.description:
Structure consisting maps of different primitive types.
Following are the Configuration Profile keys that can be passed:
    • applyConfigConstraints - Boolean - Enables configurator constraint evaluation in the solve operation.
    • applyDefaults - Boolean - Enables configurator default rules evaluation in the solve operation.
    • intentFilterInclude - List of Strings - The list of configurator Intents which should participate in the solve operation.
    • intentFilterExclude - List of Strings - The list of configurator Intents which should be ignored in the solve operation.
    • violationComputationTimeout - Integer - Indicates the max time in seconds that should be spent in violations computation.
    • minReportSeverity - Integer - Indicates the minimum report severity to be evaluated for validation failures.
    • minErrorSeverity - Integer - Indicates the minimum error severity to be evaluated for validation failures.
    • computeAllProblems - Boolean - Enables computation of all the problems of the unsat core while reporting violations.
    • minimizeProblem - Boolean - Decides if minimization of computed essential violation is required.
Struct.name: ConfigurationProfile

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation computes the available variability for a set of requested families which satisfies the input expression against the constraint(s) present in the system. The operation allows only precise expression to be passed as input in order to get the available variability for the requested families.
A precise expression represents a single product configuration and does not allow multipe values for mutually exclusive single select families. For example, if A1, A2 and A3 are values of single select family A and B1 and B2 are values of single select family B, the expression (A=A1 & B=B1) is a precise expression, whereas the following expressions are imprecise and are not supported by the operation:
1.    (A=A1 & B=B1) | (A=A2 & B=B2) - Multiple product configurations.
2.    (A=A1 | A=A2) & (B=B1 | B=B2) - Multiple feature values are selected from mutually exclusive family.
3.    A!=A3 – Expression equals (A=A1 | A=A2), that is multiple feature values selected from single select family.

If the input expression is empty, then the operation will return the available variability for the product against the constraint(s) present in the system.
The operation returns criteria status which represents the status of the configuration as part of response; the completeness of the configuration is irrespective of the families of interest and considers all the families present for the provided product context. In order to get the list of families missing valid selections for valid and incomplete configuration or details of violations for invalid configuration, the validateAndExpandExpressions service operation should be called.

Below keys are specific to the current operation:

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_skipSolutionSeverityProcessing” is set to true, the system will not compute constraint severity for each expanded expression terms. Else the system will compute constraint severity for each expanded expression terms. Computing constraint severity is performance intensive operation. Example below Use case 5 and Use case 5.1.

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_computeRangeForFreeFormFamily” is set to true, the valid range computation of free form values will be done, else valid range computation will not be done and existing range on a family without considering constraints will be returned. Example below Use case 6 and Use Case 6.1.

If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_getAllAvailableValuesPerFamily” is set to true, the system will get available values for each requested family individually after resetting clause of current family from the input expression. If user has this key set to false, the available values for each requested family are computed considering input expression as constraint. Example below Use case 7 and Use case 7.1.

This operation requires tc_ipd_config_gtwy license.

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation returns variability data for an input Configurator perspective. It allows a caller to filter the data based in input criteria.
The returned variability is comprised of one or more of the following objects configured by an input Configurator Perspective.
•    Groups (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup)
•    Families and Feature Families (Cfg0AbsOptionFamily and Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily)
•    Features and Standalone Features (Cfg0AbsOptionValue and Cfg0AbsFeature)
•    Model Families, Product Line Families and Summary Model Families (Cfg0AbsModelFamily)
•    Models (Cfg0AbsModel) including “Product Model” (Cfg0AbsProductModel), “Product Line” (Cfg0AbsProductLine), and “Summary Model” (Cfg0AbsSummaryModel)

The purpose of this SOA operation is to provide a convenient way for clients to link group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup) workspace objects with their family (Cfg0AbsFamily) workspace objects and family workspace objects with their feature (Cfg0AbsValue) workspace objects for the input configurator perspective. It also provides the corresponding allocation (Cfg0AbsAssociation) objects through which the group, family and feature objects are associated with the underlying configurator context item.
The Revision Rule in the Configurator Perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective->cfg0RevisionRule) only considers candidate revisions, that meet the following criteria:
    1.    Read Access: Candidate revisions with read access are considered for revision rule configuration.
    2.    Configuration Date: The revision date predates the rule date (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective->cfg0RevisionRule->rule_date). The relevant revision date depends on the “revision rule clause”:
        a.    “Any Status” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on the “Date Released” of the revision (WorkspaceObject->date_released)
        b.    “Selected Status” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on “Date Released” of the selected Release Status (WorkspaceObject->release_status_list->date_released)
        c.    “Working” Revision Rule clauses configure revisions based on “Creation Date” of the revision (WorkspaceObject->creation_date)
    3.    Effective Date: If the Revision Rule specifies effectivity criteria, then only candidate revisions that are effective for the given effectivity criteria are considered for configuring a valid revision. Effectivity dates can refer to the future dates. The Effectivity date is expected to specify a date later than the rule date, but the system does not enforce this expectation. You only need to configure for an effectivity date that precedes the rule date if you are making changes that are expected to take effect prior to saving these changes. For example, this can be done if you are cataloging archeological artifacts.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getVariability
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The variability data containing group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup) workspace objects linked with their family (Cfg0AbsFamily) workspace objects and family workspace objects linked with their feature (Cfg0AbsValue) workspace objects for the input configurator perspective. It also returns the corresponding allocation (Cfg0AbsAllocation) objects through which the group, family and feature objects are associated with the input configurator perspective.

The following partial errors may be returned:
    • 77073 - The operation has failed, because an invalid Configurator Perspective was passed.
    • 79010 - The operation “getVariability" expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
    • 79020 – The requestInfo has unsupported key-value pairs.

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective business object that represents a snapshot of a Product Context object. . The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.
OperationParameter.name: perspective

OperationParameter.description:
Client applications use the list of structs to specify what kind of data is to be returned for a request. It is optional. If empty, then the full variability data for the given Configurator Perspective is returned.
The valid name-values are

    • Cfg0::request:filter:Groups – Represents a Boolean value. If true, then returns the list of family group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup) objects as part of the GetVariabilityResponse->groups member. Default is true.
    • Cfg0::request:filter::Products – Represents a Boolean value. If true, then returns Product model, Product Line, Summary Models as part of the GetVariablityResponse->productFamilies member. Default is true.
    • Cfg0::request:filter:UngroupedFamilies – Represents a Boolean value. If true, the operation returns the families that are not part of any group as part of the GetVariablityResponse->ungroupedFamilies member. Default is true.
    • Cfg0::request:ViewType - Represents an Integer value. It is used to filter out auxiliary feature based on the preference value and current view Type. Valid values are - 0, 1, 3, 4 which represents the current view from which the soa is called. If no viewType is passed auxiliary features will be visible.
    •          ViewType             View
    •              0                    Variant configuration view.
    •              1                    Variability explorer view.
    •              3                    Constraints grid view.
    •              4                    Variability opened from constraints grid view.
    • ( NOTE : For explorer view auxiliary features will always be visible, Both of the constraint view 3 & 4 are handled by a common preference. )
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation validates and expands the input criteria expressions against the constraint(s) present in the system.
The operation returns criteria status which represents the status of the configuration as part of response; the completeness of the configuration; the list of families that don’t have a precise selection for incomplete configuration or details of violations for invalid configuration.
A precise selection represents a single selection for a family and does not allow multiple values for mutually exclusive single select families. For example, if A1, A2 and A3 are values of single select family A, the expression (A=A1 ) is a precise selection, whereas the following expressions are imprecise selection and family “A” will we returned as response under missingSelection :
1. (A=A1 | A=A2) - Multiple feature values are selected from a mutually exclusive family.
2. A!=A3 – Expression equals (A=A1 | A=A2), that is multiple feature values selected from a single select family.

Below keys are specific to the current operations.
If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_validateWithoutExpand” is set to true. Then operation will only validate the input expressions criteria, and output expanded expression will be empty. Criteria status will be computed in the most performant manner.
If SolveProfile keys “CFG_PROFILE_validateWithoutExpand” and “CFG_PROFILE_check_completeness” are set to true. Then operation will validate the input expressions criteria and output expanded expression is populated only if configuration is complete.
If SolveProfile key “CFG_PROFILE_skipSolutionSeverityProcessing” is set to true, the system will not compute constraint severity for each expression terms. Else the system will compute constraint severity for each expanded expression terms. Computing constraint severity is performance intensive operation. Example below Use case 6 and Use case 6.1
This operation requires tc_ipd_config_gtwy license.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::validateAndExpandExpressions

The operation returns criteria status, the completeness of the configuration, the list of families with missing the precise selection and violations for invalid configuration.

OperationParameter.description: A list of Cfg0AbsFamily families from the same product context to generate buildable combinations. The list cannot be empty and should not contain a free form family. The supported subtypes of Cfg0AbsFamily are: Cfg0AbsFeature, Cfg0AbsFeatureFamily, Cfg0AbsModelFamily and Cfg0AbsOptionFamily
OperationParameter.name: families

OperationParameter.description:
A map (string, string) of key and value pairs. Supported key and value pairs are:
• "outputFormat" - It is a buildable combination's output representation's format. Supported values are:
1. "TcFormula" : A buildable combination is represented as a teamcenter formula. It is a default format.
2. "Features" : A buildable combination is represented as a list of valid feature combinations of the input families.
• "maxSize" : It is a maximum number of the buildable combinations to generate. The default value is 10000. A value for maxSize should be less than or equal to 10000.
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description: This operation generates a list of valid configurations (configuration with optimized value for family contained in bound expression) for a given list of input families which satisfies a limiting expression. The operation returns the limiting expression’s validation status and configurations. If the limiting expression is invalid then configurations will be empty.This operation requires a tc_ipd_config_gtwy license.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::generateConfigsBasedOnOptFamily
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The response contains a limiting expression’s validation status and a list of valid configurations. ServiceData contains information about partial error details for any failures while generating configurations based on optimization family.

Following partial errors may be returned.
26025 - No Flexlm license is available for Teamcenter optional module ‘tc_ipd_config_gtwy’ and ‘config_solve_level2’.
77073 - The Configurator Perspective is invalid.
77074 - The Configurator Perspective must contain a product item.
77075 - At least one Family is expected in the input.
77143 - The JSON schema validation for “solveProfile” has failed.
77181 - The family list cannot contain free form family.
77182 - The family list cannot be empty.
77183 - The string ‘text’ is invalid key in the requestInfo. Please refer the opeation’s description for a valid input key.
77184 - The value ‘text’ is invalid for the key ‘text’ in the requestInfo. Please refer the opeation’s description for valid input.
256021 - The string ‘text’ cannot be converted into an expression.
256055 - The provided solve profile is invalid.
256059 - The input solve profile JSON is invalid because it consists of duplicate key.
256068 - The input bound expression is invalid. The Bound Expression should refer to Numeric Families with Literal Value.
256069 - The input solve profile is invalid. Current operation supports only fatal severity constraints.
256070 - A Valid Configuration exists outside the upper bound. Try with bigger bound value.
256071 - A Valid Configuration exists outside the lower bound. Try with smaller bound value.
256065 - The operation ‘text’ has failed, because of free-form family ‘text’. Free-form families are not allowed to generate buildable combinations.
77100 - The value ‘text’ for the family ‘text’ is invalid or not configured.
77023 - No Family ‘text’ with the namespace ‘text’ can be found.

OperationParameter.description: A structure that defines the inputs required for generating configurations based optimization familiy. It includes a runtime perspective snapshot, a solve profile for constraint evaluation, optional limiting for filtering configurations, bound expressions, a flag to determine optimization direction (maximum or minimum), and a list of valid product families to compute the configurations.
OperationParameter.name: configInput

OperationParameter.description:
A list of key and value pairs(string, string). Supported key and value pairs are:
•    “outputFormat” – It is a buildable combination’s output representation’s format. Supported values are:
1.    “TcFormula” : A configuration is represented as a teamcenter formula. It is a default format.
2.    “Features” : A configuration is represented as a list of valid feature combinations of the input families.
•    “maxSize” : It is a maximum number of the configurations to generate. The default value is 1. A value for maxSize should be in the range of 1 to 10000.
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation converts the input variant expression list from Teamcenter formula format to JSON format or vice versa based on the expression format requested.

The JSON string of the variant expression adheres to the JSON schema for variant expression defined in VariantExpression_Schema.json located in %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema.The “Teamcenter formula format” is published in the Teamcenter technical documentation.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::convertVariantExpressions
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
Returns the list of formulae or variant expressions in JSON format for the corresponding input variant expressions or Teamcenter formula respectively. If operation fails to convert any variant formula or equivalently for an input variant expression, a partial error is returned for the same and the processing continues for the next object in the list.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    77073 - The Configurator Perspective is invalid.
•    77074 - The Configurator Perspective must contain a product item.
•    77143 - The operation “convertVariantExpressions” has failed to retrieve output variant expression for the input expression at index ‘n’ due to the JSON schema validation failure.
•    79014 - Some or all of the key-value pairs in the list of request info pairs sent to the operation "convertVariantExpressions" are unsupported: ""{ key=invalidkey1 : values = [ invalidvalue1 ]}". Please report this error to your system administrator.
•    79018 - The operation “convertVariantExpressions” has failed to retrieve output variant expressions for the input variant expression at index ‘n’. due to formula validation failure.

OperationParameter.description: A Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective object that represents a snapshot of a Product Context object.
OperationParameter.name: perspective

OperationParameter.description: A list of variant expressions that either adhere to Teamcenter formula format or to the JSON schema for ApplicationConfigExpression defined in VariantExpression_Schema.json located in %TC_DATA%/json/variabilityadaptor/schema. All the inputs in the list should adhere to only one of the above two formats in a single operation request. The operation will return partial error for the invalid input indices.
OperationParameter.name: variantExpressions

OperationParameter.description:
The expressionFormat represents a string to indicate the expected format of the output variant expression.
Valid values are:
“json_grid” – Input format should be Teamcenter formula format and output format will be variant expression in JSON format. If any of the inputs do not adhere to Teamcenter formula format the operation will return partial error for the invalid input indices.
“tc_formula” – Input format should be variant expression in JSON format and output format will be Teamcenter formula text. If any of the inputs do not adhere to the JSON format specified the operation will return partial error mentioning invalid input indices.
OperationParameter.name: expressionFormat

OperationParameter.description: A list of request names and value pairs. This is reserved for future use.
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description:
Retrieves an array of Configurator rules for a given configurator perspective, based on the criteria as specified below.

You can specify abstract or concrete classes for filtering, all of which must be subtypes of Cfg0AbsRule.

List of families and features referenced in a rule’s expression. The type of the expression can be either 'condition' or 'subject'.
The families or features may be referenced in the expression using the logical operators 'AND', 'OR', or 'NOT'. Depending on the requirement, all or any of the families and features in this list may need to be referenced in the expression for the constraint to qualify for the output list. The expression may reference additional families or features beyond those in the input list.
If you specify that all the input families or features need to be referenced in the rule's condition expression and if one or more families or features from this list are not referenced, then the constraint will not qualify for output. If you specify that any of the input families or features can be referenced to in the rule's condition expression, the constraint will qualify if any of the input families or features are present in the constraint's condition expression.
The same search process is applied when searching families and features in a subject expression.

For rules of the type Cfg0AbsFreeFormRule, their features and families are considered as the subject.

A saved query with a list of persistent attributes and their values. These attributes can be either custom attributes or out-of-the-box (OOTB) attributes.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::searchConstraints
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The operation returns a search constraint response.

Following partial errors may be returned.
3005 - Invalid attribute 'text' found for query.
3020 - No value was specified for this query.
3040 - This query cannot be executed.
77073 - The Configurator Perspective is invalid.
77199 - Input to the property 'text' for "searchConditions" should be of type 'Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue' or Cfg0AbsRule
79014 - Some or all of the key-value pairs in the list of request info pairs sent to the operation "text" are unsupported: "text". Please report this error to your system administrator.

OperationParameter.description: A Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective is a runtime business object representing a snapshot of a Configurator Product Context object. The ownership of the runtime object is with the calling application and ultimately with the client since all the server layers are stateless.
OperationParameter.name: perspective

OperationParameter.description: A list of rule type names. Objects corresponding to these rule types will be returned. If the list is empty, objects of all rule types will be returned. Note that the object needs to be a subtype of Cfg0AbsRule.
OperationParameter.name: ruleTypes

OperationParameter.description: A list of families and features that are part of the condition expression. The object must be a subtype of either Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue.
OperationParameter.name: conditions

OperationParameter.description: A list of families and features that are part of the subject expression. The object must be subtype of either Cfg0AbsFamily or Cfg0AbsValue.
OperationParameter.name: subject

OperationParameter.description: A QueryInput. This is an optional parameter for a saved search query. When executed, the query should return an object of the type Cfg0AbsRule. The query can be based on the out-of-the-box (OOTB) attributes of Cfg0AbsRule or any custom attributes of custom classes. The operation intersects the result of the query with the results of other criteria specified in this operation, such as ruleTypes, conditions, and subject. This means the final result is based on both the query and these additional criteria. Please refer to the use cases for examples. If this parameter is not specified, the operation will search based on other input parameter criteria.
OperationParameter.name: queryInput

OperationParameter.description:
A list of KeyValuePair. This is an optional input parameter. Supported key is ‘matchAllObjects’. This key is used to search for a rule based on whether all or anyof the input conditions or subject need to be present in the rule’s conditions or subject respectively. The valid values are:
•    true :    All specified conditions and subject need to be present in the rule’s conditions and subjects. This is a default value.
•    false :    Any of the specifed subject and condtions is present in the rule’s conditions and subjects
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description: This operation created or update the variant criteria object. Any object which has variant behavior implemented can be used as an variant criteria object. If parameter <font face="courier" height="10">saveRule</font> is set as FALSE then variant criteria object is not saved and transient object is returned. The relationship name used to associate the variant criteria object to the product Item.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::createUpdateVariantRules
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: The list of SOA structure with instances (either created or updated) of objects acting as variant criteria along with variant expression information.

OperationParameter.description: List of variant rule input structures.
OperationParameter.name: rules

OperationParameter.description: The revision rule to use to retrieve the correct revisions of the option data referenced by the expressions.
OperationParameter.name: revRule

OperationTemplate.description: This operation converts the input variant expressions of boolean expression format into displayable or user readable format.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getVariantExpressionDisplayStrings
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The converted expression display string for the given inputs. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.
    • 256041 - Product configuration type cannot have attributes '', 'revRuleClientId' and a element 'revisionRule'. Only one should be specified.
    • 77034 - The supported variant expression types for the object "Rule 01" of type "Default Rule" are 27,33. An Invalid variant expression types provided : 38

OperationParameter.description: The revision rule to use to retrieve the correct revisions of the option data referenced by the expressions.

OperationTemplate.description:
This internal operation returns the family group instances. The parameter context may provide either the product item(s).
If the product item(s) of context is available then those instances of the family group (Cfg0AbsFamilyGroup or subtypes) are returned which are allocated to the given product item(s).
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getFamilyGroups
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The list of group objects and their corresponding allocation objects are returned in response structure. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.
    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided in parameter context

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective instance to specify the product item(s) or product model(s) for which the family groups are requested.
OperationParameter.name: context

OperationTemplate.description:
This internal operation returns the option family instances given context information. If the product item(s) member is provided in context, then the option families that are allocated to any of the specified product item(s) are returned. If the product models member is provided in context, then the option families that are made available to at least one of given the product model(s) are returned.

In addition, to filter the option families further, the 'groups' input parameter can be leveraged. If this parameter is populated with the family group instances or IDs, then the option families that are allocated to any of the specified product item(s) and which are members of the specified family group instances are returned.
If the parameter 'otherFamilies' is set to 'true', then operation will return that option families which are not the members of any family group instances however are allocated to at least one of the specified product item(s).
The default value for this parameter is 'false', which guides the system to only return the Option Families from the Family Groups specified in the input parameter 'groups'.
If parameter 'unavailableFamilies' is set to true, option families those are the members of any of the specified groups and are allocated to specified product context are returned even if their availability rule is in an 'unavailable' state.

Note: In Teamcenter 10.1.2 the product model(s) member of context is ignored.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getOptionFamilies
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The list of structures, that encapsulate the information about a Family Group and the list of families it contains, along with the allocation objects which allocate the families to the respective product items. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.

    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided in parameter context

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective instance to specify the product item(s) or the product model(s) for which the family groups are requested.
OperationParameter.name: context

OperationParameter.description: The list of family group instances. This parameter is optional. If specified, only the families which are members of the specified family groups within the specified context are returned.
OperationParameter.name: groups

OperationParameter.description:
If this parameter is set to true, the families those are not the members of any family group within the specified context are returned.
The default value for this parameter is false, which guides the operation to return the families only from the specified family groups.
Note: This functionality is not supported in the Teamcenter 10.1.2 release.
OperationParameter.name: otherFamilies

OperationParameter.description:
If this parameter is set to true, the option families those are members of any of the specified groups and are allocated to specified product context are returned even if their availability rule is in an 'unavailable' state.
Default value for this parameter is false.
Note: This functionality is not supported in the Teamcenter 10.1.2 release.
OperationParameter.name: unavailableFamilies

OperationTemplate.description:
This internal service operation returns the feature instances based on the specified context and other parameters. If product item(s) member is provided in the context, then the features that are allocated to any of the product items are returned. If product model(s) member is provided in the context, then the features that are made available to any of the product models are returned.
If groups parameter is populated with the family group instances, then only those feature instances which belong to the family instances of given list of family group members are returned.
If families parameter is populated with the family instances, then only those feature instances which belong to the given family instances are returned.
If unavailableValues is set to 'true', it would also return the features which are marked with negative availability.

Note: In Teamcenter 10.1.2 the product model(s) member in context is not considered. This member is used for availability feature and this feature will be supported in Teamcenter 10.1.3 onwards.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getOptionValues
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The list of features along with their availability in product model. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.
    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided in parameter context

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective instance to specify the product item(s) or product model(s) for which the rule objects are requested.
OperationParameter.name: context

OperationParameter.description: Optional list of family groups. If specified, only the features belonging to any of the <font face="courier" height="10">families</font>, which are members of the specified family groups are returned.
OperationParameter.name: groups

OperationParameter.description: Optional list of families. If specified, only the features belonging to any of the specified families are returned.
OperationParameter.name: families

OperationParameter.description:
If this parameter is set to true, the values which are marked with negative availability would also be returned. Default value for this parameter is 'false'.
Note: This functionality is not supported in the Teamcenter 10.1.2 release.
OperationParameter.name: unavailableValues

OperationTemplate.description: Gets the results of applying default rules to a set of input expressions in the context of the associated Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective objects.

The updated expression containing defaults. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.
    • 79007 - This operation expects at least one Product Item in the Configurator Perspective object.

A list of ProductDeafultsInput structures each of which comprises a list of BusinessObjectConfigExpression.Each ProductDeafultsInput structure represents its own transaction and partial error boundary.Providing fewer ProductDeafultsInput structures where each comprises many BusinessObjectConfigExpressions is more efficient than providing
many ProductDeafultsInput structures where each comprises a few BusinessObjectConfigExpressions. However, the latter returns more granular partial errors.

Use this operation if data model changes in a higher Teamcenter release make it impossible to use offline data replication. OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getVariantCache
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The variant cache data for the given product item. The partial errors are returned in serviceData.
    • 256041 - Product configuration type cannot have attributes 'revRuleName', 'revRuleClientId' and 'RevisionRule' together. Only one should be specified.

OperationParameter.description: The product context ItemRevision which has the variability data defined. If client does not have instance product item, in that case parameter productItemId can be used.
OperationParameter.name: productItem

OperationParameter.description: Revision rule
OperationParameter.name: revRule

OperationParameter.description: The UID of the product model.
OperationParameter.name: productModelUID

OperationParameter.name: productItemUID

OperationTemplate.description:
Executes a search based on a search recipe. The search results can contain any sub-types of POM_Object. The search recipe could be a complex search definition that combines multiple simpler search definitions in a logical sequence, e.g. multiple saved queries as defined in the Teamcenter application QueryBuilder.

The search is executed in the context of a configurator perspective (Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective). Configurator objects such as features, or constraint rules, are filtered based on their relationship to the product context items and product models in the configurator perspective.

Variant and effecitvity configurable objects in the search results are filtered according to the criteria associated with the VariantRule and RevisionRule in the configurator perspective.

Revisable objects in the search results are revision configured according to the RevisionRule in the configurator perspective.

The results of a search are returned in batches based on the defaultLoadCount specified in the search options. A search cursor object is returned in the response with which subsequent batches can be requested with operation fetchNextSearchResults.

Search options may be used to sort the results of a search using one or more attributes of the returned objects.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::executeSearch
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The found objects and the search cursor object for retrieving next set of objects. The partial errors are returned for following case

    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided.
    • 79008 - The search criteria provided in input is invalid.

OperationParameter.description: Recipe for executing the search
OperationParameter.name: searchRecipe

OperationParameter.description: Search Options for a given Search (load count and sorting)
OperationParameter.name: searchOptions

OperationTemplate.description: This operation gets the next set of objects in the search result of a previously executed search. The returned results will be based on the load count specified in the SearchCursor input structure.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::fetchNextSearchResults
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: Returns the <font face="courier" height="10">SearchResponse</font> structure (next chunk of search result, search cursor and partial errors)

OperationParameter.description: A runtime object identifier that keeps track of the Search results and the corresponding indexes as of where the caller has consumed the results
OperationParameter.name: searchCursor

OperationParameter.description: Count of next set of objects to be loaded. The value can be different from the cfg0Count in Cfg0SearchCursor.
OperationParameter.name: loadCount

OperationTemplate.description:
Validates the given expression by applying the constraint rules and returns violations and an updated expression resulting from the application of include rules that can be set on the expression.

The value of TC_Default_Solve_Type preference is used for using solve type for this operation.

Values for applyConstraints are as integrated as follows
1 //enable configurator constraint evaluation
+ 8 //report warnings in addition to errors
+ 16 //also report informational messages
+ 32 //don't stop if a violation is encountered
+ 256 //skip the check against _allocated_ variability which could raise a
    "k_variant_criteria_outside" validation failure
+ 1024 //skip criteria update based on validation rules (For example configurator exclusion rule). If this flag is not set then the operation will update the variant criteria after applying validation rules.
+ 2048 //enable Availability Constraint evaluation.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::validateProductConfiguration
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The list of violations and an updated expression with selections due to constraint application. The partial errors are returned in serviceData in following cases.
    • 79007 - At least one Product Item in the Perspective object is required for this operation.
    • 77034 - The supported variant expression types for the object "Rule 01" of type "Default Rule" are 27 and 33. Invalid variant expression types provided : 28

OperationParameter.description:
A list of ValidateProductConfigInput structures each of which comprises a list of BusinessObjectConfigExpression.Each ValidateProductConfigInput structure represents its own transaction and partial error boundary.Providing fewer ValidateProductConfigInput structures where each comprises many BusinessObjectConfigExpressions is more efficient than providing
many ValidateProductConfigInput structures where each comprises a few BusinessObjectConfigExpressions. However, the latter returns more granular partial errors.
OperationParameter.name: inputs

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation splits the given input expressions into the list of model and option condition expressions.
The business object type of the Cfg0AbsValue value objects, with which the input expressions are formed, divides these values into a set of Cfg0AbsModel objects and a set of Cfg0AbsOptionValue objects. This operation decomposes each input expression into a two lists. One expression list that is formed exclusively with Cfg0AbsModel objects and other expression list that is formed exclusively with Cfg0AbsOptionValue objects.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Internal::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getModelAndOptionConditions
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
Returns the list of the model and the option condition expressions for the given input expressions.
The following partial errors may be returned:
79009 - An invalid configuration perspective is passed to the operation.
79010 - The operation expects one product item in the configuration perspective.

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective instance to specify the context and revision rule. If configurator perspective is provided by each input structure in list inputStructs, then this operationConfigPerspective parameter can be NULL.
OperationParameter.name: operationConfigPerspective

OperationParameter.description: The input structure for getModelAndOptionConditions operation. Each entry in this list defines a partial error boundary.
OperationParameter.name: inputStructs

OperationTemplate.description: This operation determines and returns the degree of overlap between a set of configuration expressions and a reference configuration expression.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getOverlapStates
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
Overlap information is returned separately for each of the input structure. The degree of overlap between each expression in the input structure and the corresponding reference expression in the same input structure is indicated with an overlap state keyword. This following illustrates possible scenarios:

VariantRule: . . .|---------------|
Object 0: .|----|. . . . . . . . . . . . . . : k_overlapstate_none
Object 1: . . |------| . . . . . . . . . . . : k_overlapstate_intersect
Object 2: . . . . . . . .|----|. . . . . . . : k_overlapstate_subset
Object 3: . . . . . . . . . .|------|. . . . : k_overlapstate_intersect
Object 4: .|-----------------------------| . : k_overlapstate_superset
Object 5: . . . . |---------------|. . . . . : k_overlapstate_match
Object 6: . . . . |-------------------|. . . : k_overlapstate_superset
Object 7: . . |-------------------|. . . . . : k_overlapstate_superset
Object 8: . . . . . . . FALSE. . . . . . . . : k_overlapstate_none
Object 9: . . . . . . . TRUE . . . . . . . . : k_overlapstate_superset

The following partial errors may be returned:
    • 79007 - At least one product item should be provided in parameter context
    • 256000 - An internal configurator error occurred.
    • 256001 - A general configurator error occurred.
    • 256002 - The following product is invalid: [DictionaryNamespace]FamilyName (Context: info).
    • 256003 - The following feature value is invalid: [DictionaryNamespace]FamilyName (Context: info).
    • 256004 - The following feature family is invalid: [DictionaryNamespace]FamilyName (Context: info).
    • 256005 - An invalid feature combination was found (Context: info).
    • 256006 - An invalid product configuration was found (Context: info).
    • 256007 - An invalid expression was found (Context: info).
    • 256008 - The following Boolean operator is invalid: opcode (Context: info).
    • 256010 - A time-out occurred (Context: info).
    • 256011 - A resource is not available (Context: info).
    • 256013 - A configurator implementation specific error occurred (Context: info).
    • 256014 - The expression contains unmatched quote at position 'number'.
    • 256015 - The expression contains unmatched bracket at position 'number'.
    • 256016 - An unexpected token 'text' was found at position 'number'.
    • 256017 - The entry 'text' was found at position 'number' when an option value was expected.
    • 256018 - The token 'text' is missing after 'text' at position 'number'.
    • 256019 - The expression adaptor does not support text used at position 'number'.
    • 256020 - The XML tag 'text' has no text value.
    • 256021 - The string 'formula' cannot be converted into an expression.
    • 256022 - The operator code 'opcode' in token at position 'number' is unknown.
    • 256023 - The value 'text' in token at position 'number' is unknown.
    • 256024 - The family 'text' in token at position 'number' is unknown.
    • 256025 - An ambiguous option value name 'FamilyName' in namespace 'DictionaryNamespace' in token at position 'number' was found: text.
    • 256026 - An ambiguous option family name 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' was found: 'text'.
    • 256027 - The option namespace 'DictionaryNamespace' in token at position 'number' is invalid.
    • 256028 - The option family 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' is invalid.
    • 256029 - The option value 'text' for family 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' is invalid.
    • 256030 - The option value 'text' for family 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' is invalid: its value is not numeric.
    • 256031 - The option value 'text' for family 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' is invalid: the value unit of measure 'text' does not match the family unit of measure 'text'.
    • 256032 - The option / family / family namespace combination 'text' / 'FamilyName' / 'DictionaryNamespace' in token at position 'number' is invalid.
    • 256033 - The family 'FamilyName' for option / family namespace combination 'text' / 'DictionaryNamespace' in token at position 'number' is invalid.
    • 256034 - There is no option value in token at position 'number'.
    • 256035 - The option value 'text' for family 'FamilyName' in token at position 'number' is invalid: the value is not a valid date.

OperationParameter.description: The Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective instance to specify the product item(s) in which context the overlap state should be determined.
OperationParameter.name: context

OperationParameter.description: Specifies the set of input structures each of which defines a set of expression and the reference expression for which the degree of overlap should be determined.
OperationParameter.name: overlapStateInputs

OperationTemplate.description: This operation computes the available features within a set of requested families. The parameters criteriaExpression and familiesToTest are used to pass in the input expression and families of interest requesting the available features. The operation in response returns the available product variability for the requested families satisfying the input expression in criteriaExpression and the constraint(s) present in the system. If the input parameter criteriaExpression is empty, then the response will return the product variability for the requested families satisfying all the system constraints. If the requested family list is empty, the operation will not return any variability information.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getAvailableProductVariability
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
A list of features, default values, value ranges, violations and/or the suggested expression satisfying input expression and the set of constraints present in the configurator context.

The following partial errors may be returned:

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation process cells of Expression matrix expressionMatrix to validate satisfiability of Expression(s) against optional scope Expression(s). Expression matrix row(s) represents Expressions(s) to validate and column(s) represent scope Expression(s). So each cell in the Expression matrix represents a combination of two expressions, one is referred to as an “Expression to validate” the other as a “Scope Expressions”.

Cell(s) of the Expression matrix to be process for validation operation are determined with matrixSubset which is a list of cells of Expression matrix. Validation operation also does the application of the constraint rules such as inclusion rule, exclusion rule or availability rule for the Configurator Perspective.

This operation retrieves the Product Configurator configuration session information from the sessionConfigObj object that is marked to carry such information. A operation user starts a Product Configurator session to create product configurations using configuration features. The session holds product information such as the, Cfg0ConfContext, RevisionRule, Effectivity, Rule Date. The product information is also represented as Cfg0ConfiguratorPerspective object. The product information configures the features which user can select to build product configuration. The session also holds parameters called as Configuration Profile which govern the evaluation of configurator constraints during validation and expansion of the product configuration. sessionConfigObj must implement ConfigurationSession behavior, so that Product Configurator configuration session information can be attached and retrieved from them. For example operation caller can use VariantRule or Cfg0AbsConfiguratorCriteria type of objects to which they can attach required Configuration session information.
The operation response conveys the information about the status of the configuration and independent set of constraint rules which are responsible together for conflict to occur.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::validateProductConditions
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
Operation Response structure is as below:
o The response conveys errors occurred during operation with service data with index of input Expression(s) and client identifier of Expression(s).
o A validation operation output data and identification information to correlate it with operation input. Identification information is client identifiers for both expression to validate and scope expression.
o Validation operation output has criteria status and conflict information.

Correlation Information for input to output structure:
o Index of list of CellValidationResult structure instances has associated entry from operation input matrixSubset list of cells.
o CellValidationResult structure member cellClientIDs pair of string’s first member represents client ID of expression to validate and second member represents client ID of Scope Expression. This pair can be used to correlate between operation input and output.

The following partial errors may be returned:

o 79009 - An invalid configuration perspective is passed to the operation “validateProductConditions ".
o 79010 - The operation " validateProductConditions" expects one product item in the configuration perspective.
o 256054 - The value for the Constraint Application bit pattern is invalid.

OperationParameter.name: sessionConfigObj

OperationParameter.description: It is a structure of two list of expressions where the first list represents the row headers of an Expression matrix and the second list represents the columns headers of an Expression matrix. Each cell in the Expression matrix represents a combination of two expressions, one is referred to as “Expression to validate” the other as “Scope Expressions”. A validation checks the satisfiability of the AND combination of the two expressions for each cell in the context of all configurator constraints.
OperationParameter.name: expressionMatrix

OperationParameter.description: Specifies the subset of cells in the “expressionMatrix” to validate. The subset is identified as a pair of row and column indexes.
OperationParameter.name: matrixSubset

OperationTemplate.description:
The Service operation expects a user to provide a set of configurations which are to be checked for validity and completeness. The service operation also returns a set of configurations which are unknown to the user.

These configurations are passed to and returned by the service operation via a ‘Roster Table’.

A ‘Roster Table’ is used to represent configurations. A ‘Roster Table’ is capable of storing configurations. A configuration record in ‘Roster Table’ is similar to saved variant rule. ‘Roster Table’ consists of two parts,

1.    Column Headers – A list of config expressions, one for each column in the table. A config expression is used to identify family name, family namespace, value and operator. Example: In the config Expression “[Teamcenter]A=A1”, family name is A, namespace is “Teamcenter”, operator is “=” and operand is “A1”.

2.    Rows – Rows store multiple row. A row contains a configuration, just like a Saved Variant Rule. The configuration is stored in a bit string, which means it can only contain ‘0’ or ‘1’. The total length of bit string is twice the number of columns present in ‘Roster Table’. Hence a string representing a cell has a size of 2. Given string can only have either ‘0’ or ‘1’ the following strings can represent a cell. They are described below with their logical meaning
    a.    ‘00’ – Both True and False conditions are possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    b.    ‘01’ – Only True condition is possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    c.    ‘10’ – Only False Condition is possible for corresponding column header config Expression.
    d.    ‘11’ - Not Defined

A user input consisting of one/more configurations is passed to the service operation using ‘Roster Table’. These configurations are checked by the service operation for validity and completeness. An input ‘Roster Table’ is said to be complete if the input ‘Roster Table’ passed by user is able to represent all the possible combinations given no constraint is violated.

User has ability to provide scope to the service operation while doing completeness check. This is done by passing a list of families. Only families present in the list are used by the service operation to compute the possible combinations and then evaluate whether the passed configurations via input ‘Roster Table’ are able to cover each and every one of them.

User also has an ability to provide ‘explicit families’ to service operation. When a configuration from input ‘Roster Table’ is checked for validity turns out to be ‘invalid’ then service operation checks weather the reason for its invalidity is due to a family present in ‘explicit families’. If yes, then exception conditions on those family is checked, if we find an exception condition that meets the configuration input this implies the exception condition allows the configuration to be valid.

Given all configurations passed via input ‘Roster Table’ are valid, and they are able to represent all possible combinations then input is said to be complete. If they don’t the configurations passed via input ‘Roster Table’ are termed incomplete. Missing configurations are computed by service operation and returned via output ‘Roster Table’

If some but not all configuration passed by user via ‘Roster Table’ is found to be invalid, this means that the configuration wasn’t able to satisfy constraints present in the system. User can specify severity of constraints which will participate in evaluating the configurations in input ‘Roster Table’. These invalid configurations are communicated back to the user and missing configurations are evaluated using valid configurations present in input ‘Roster Table’.

If all the configurations passed to the service operation are invalid the service operation will return empty output ‘Roster Table’.

Use Case 1:
A product context has 3 Boolean Families ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’.

These 3 families can create a total of 8 configurations given there is no constraint in the system.

A user can use ‘getConfigurationRosterCoverage’ service operation to pass 3 configuration among the 8 possible via input ‘Roster Table’.

In the current example all the 8 configurations are possible but the user only passed 3 of them in input. Hence the service operation provides verdict as ‘valid’ for all the 3 input configurations. The remaining 5 configurations are returned back to user via output ‘Roster Table’. Additionally service operation also returns a verdict of ‘incomplete’ to user as he missed 5 possible configurations in input ‘Roster Table’.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::getConfigurationRosterCoverage
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
Output structure tells user which combinations passed in input via ‘Roster Table’ were valid and which were invalid. Additionally if also informs user how a correction can be made to an invalid input configuration such that it becomes a valid configuration.

The following partial errors may be returned:
•    79001 - The operation has encountered an internal error.

OperationParameter.description: Contains input required to perform solution completeness check for a given set of combinations.
OperationParameter.name: configurationRoster

OperationTemplate.description:
•    The generateCondensedTelemetry service operation retrieves a large dataset from the data grid and processes it into a smaller subset, which is used to generate a configurator data snapshot. Data grid is a key-value store database.
•    This condensed telemetry data is then posted back to the data grid for snapshot generation.
•    The resulting snapshot provides downstream users with consistent configurator data, enabling faster response times and improved user experience.
•    At present, the end user cannot see the condensed telemetry data on the data grid.

Overview when the service operation is executed successfully:
•    When the data condensation for the specified time interval is successful, the condensed telemetry data is posted to the data grid. The data grid will store this condensed telemetry data, which will later be used in subsequent operations for snapshot generation.
•    Once the condensed telemetry data is posted to the data grid, the server will track the number of jobs that have been posted for snapshot generation. This count is returned in the service operation response under the parameter "numberOfJobs."
•    Absence of any partial errors in serviceData represents the successful completion of the service operation.

Overview when the service operation execution fails:
•    If the service operation fails for any reason, no data will be posted to the data grid. The value "numberOfJobs" will be returned as 0.
•    The serviceData will have the partial errors to indicate the failure of the service operation.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::generateCondensedTelemetry
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The operation will return a structure specifying the status of the operation and number of jobs to be processed for snapshot generation.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    77089 - The request to compile a Configurator Rule Set was not processed, because the specified date “startTime” represents a date in the future. Please use a date before the current date "2024-11-14T00:00:00Z ".
•    77213 - The request to compile a Configurator Rule Set was not processed, because the specified date “startTime” is greater than “endTime”.

OperationParameter.description:
This parameter indicates the time from which unprocessed data is to be retrieved from a data grid. This data will be processed into a smaller subset i.e. condensed form.
The format is in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
The time is closed interval.
If the startTime is not provided, the time interval will be determined based on the Teamcenter preference i.e. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval.
Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval takes string value in the format of PnYnMnDTnHnMnS as defined in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
OperationParameter.name: startTime

OperationParameter.description:
This parameter indicates the time up to which unprocessed data is to be retrieved from a data grid. This data will be processed into a smaller subset i.e. condensed form.
The format is in ISO 8601 format https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
The time is closed interval.
If the endTime is not provided, the time interval will be determined based on a Teamcenter preference i.e. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval. Cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval takes string value in the format of PnYnMnDTnHnMnS as defined in ISO 8601 https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601
OperationParameter.name: endTime

OperationParameter.description: A map (string, list of string). This is reserved for future use.
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description:
•    The generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operation retrieves the condensed telemetry data from the data grid and processes it to generate a configurator snapshot. Data grid is a key-value store database.
•    The generated configurator snapshot is posted back to the data grid.
•    Each service operation will be assigned one telemetry job from the data grid and processes it to generate configurator snapshot. There will be parallel invocation of generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot service operations to multiple servers.
•    The configurator snapshot enables the downstream users to work with a pre-processed constant or frozen configurator data. This enables improved performance for validate and expand action.

The service operation retrieves a job from the data grid based on priority, as determined by the generateCondensedTelemetry service operation. A job corresponds to a single row in the data grid, containing condensed telemetry data used to generate the configurator snapshot.

Each job in the data grid has a status value of "Pending," indicating that it is available for processing. The service operation will be assigned one of these "Pending" jobs for processing.

The assignment of a job to the service operation is not based on any input to the service operation. Therefore, the service operation does not take any input parameters except requestInfo.

Overview when the service operation is executed successfully:
•    The service operation retrieves a specific row of condensed telemetry data from the data grid. This row of condensed telemetry is called a ‘job’.
•    If the job retrieval is successful, the data grid is updated for that particular row. This update helps to determine which job will be selected from the data grid for snapshot generation in the next service operation request by another server.
•    The server generates a snapshot for the retrieved job. After each successful job completion, the status of the job on the data grid will be marked as complete.
•    If there are any more unprocessed jobs on the data grid then in the response, the value of moreJobsExist is true, more service operations are to be invoked. If false, no more service operations are to be invoked.

Overview when the service operation execution fails:
•    The service operation will retrieve a specific row of condensed telemetry data from the data grid. This row of condensed telemetry is called a ‘job’.
•    If job retrieval fails due to the absence of unprocessed jobs in the data grid, the moreJobsExist value will be set to false, along with an error in the serviceData. For any other unexpected failure, an appropriate error will be reported in the serviceData.
•    The server will try to generate a snapshot for the retrieved job. In case of failure, the status of the job on the data grid will be not be marked as complete. In this case, the job is again available for processing by the next service operation request.
•    If a job is taking more time than what is defined in the preference cfg0DefaultTelemetryTimeInterval then it will be marked as ‘timed out’.
•    If a job is getting failed for a maximum 5 number of times then it will be marked as ‘timed out’ in the data grid. The timed out jobs will not be picked by the service operation for processing.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::generateTelemetryBasedSnapshot
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The operation will return a structure specifying whether there are any more pending jobs on the data grid.

Following partial errors may be returned:
•    77214 - There are no unprocessed jobs on the data grid.

OperationParameter.description: A map (string, list of string). This is reserved for future use.
OperationParameter.name: requestInfo

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation expands and updates the respective variants (VariantRule) by incorporating expanded expressions, validation and completeness status.
The configurator constraints are filtered based on the solve profile present in the session information of the respective variants for the expand operation.
Variants without write access will be skipped during expansion, and such Variants are reported.
OperationTemplate.name: Cfg0::Soa::Configurator::ConfiguratorManagement::expandAndUpdateVariants
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
The following partial errors may be returned.

Error Code:
•    77104 - Input object contains incorrect config profile information .
•    515001 - Input object does not have WRITE access for the current user.
•    257005 - Input object is not of type or sub-type of VariantRule.
